News.title: Moment unruly passenger gets duct-taped in seat after ‘hurling abuse at crew’ in midair meltdown forcing plane to divert
News.content:
AIR TANTRUM Moment unruly passenger gets duct-taped in seat after ‘hurling abuse at crew’ in midair meltdown forcing plane to divert

THIS is the wild moment a deranged passenger is duct-taped to his seat after allegedly hurling abuse at fellow flyers and crew.

An American airlines flight from Dallas, Texas to Newark, New Jersey was plunged into chaos – with shocking photos showing the aftermath.



At around 10:15pm a man exploded into an unhinged diatribe littered with racist and homophobic slurs at his seatmate beside him.

While spiralling into a hate-fuelled meltdown, the man even lashed out physically – allegedly striking his fellow flyer and smashing his laptop.



A woman tried to intervene in the mid-air tantrum on Thursday but was allegedly pushed back by the suspected fiend – prompting three men to jump in and help.

When a black flight attendant approached the individual – he shouted more racial slurs, according to reporting by TMZ.

Airline crew handed the three passengers duct tape and zipties – and the flyers then reportedly tied the man to his seat while he battled back.

The plane was even forced to divert to Baltimore to deal with the disruption.

Crew and passengers resorted to extreme measures to stop the alleged hate attacks – and emerged with several rolls of thick duct tape.

Shocking photos show the man strapped to his seat with multiple strips of tape criss-crossing over his face and chest.



His hands were also bound in the sticky adhesive, as well as being clamped together with two yellow zip ties.

Blood appears to be visible on his arm, thought it is unclear how he sustained the possible injuries.

American Airlines told NY Post that the flight was diverted to Baltimore “due to a disruptive customer”.

They added that when the plane landed “law enforcement met the aircraft and assisted with deplaning the customer before the flight continued to its destination.”

The man has been arrested and the FBI has said they are currently conducting interviews to determine if the man will face federal charges.



There have been more than 1,160 “unruly passenger incidents” so far in 2026, according to the Federal Aviation Administration.

On New Year’s Day, a plane was diverted after a man allegedly launched into a racist rant against fellow flyers.

The enraged passenger allegedly hurled bigoted abuse at the two people next to him – believed to be of Indian or Pakistani descent.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Anjou Ahlborn Kay, a passenger, shared the footage on Facebook where she described the man as “bigoted” and “disturbing”.

When the attendant asks him to calm down, the frustrated man can be heard saying: “I’m perfectly calm. I’m not yelling, you want to hear me f*****g yelling?”

News.title: Dramatic moment US blitzes three Iranian oil tankers after ‘ballistic missiles launched towards navy warships’
News.content:
THIS is the dramatic moment US forces blast three Iranian oil tankers after missiles were reportedly launched towards navy warships.

US Central Command (CENTCOM) said it “permanently disabled” M/T Downy off the coast of Iran’s Kharg Island and M/T Stark 1 near Jask, east of the Strait of Hormuz.



American forces also “completely destroyed” the unladen crude oil carrier M/T Kylo in the Gulf of Oman, CENTCOM said.

The statement, posted on X, said the tankers were part of a shadow network funding Iran’s Revolutionary Guard and its armed proxies.





CENTCOM shared dramatic footage of what it said were the strikes.

Massive blasts erupt across three different vessels before bursting into flames.

Blazes rage across the ships as huge plumes of thick black smoke billow into the sky.

CENTCOM said the strikes came after the IRGC launched ballistic missiles toward two US Navy warships patrolling regional waters.



A US aircraft carrier and guided-missile destroyer successfully evaded “multiple unprovoked Iranian attacks”, according to CENTCOM.

No US personnel were hurt, it added.

CENTCOM commander Admiral Brad Cooper said: “Let the message to the IRGC be clear: If you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost – taking out three of yours.

“We will not hesitate to defend American forces, and if necessary, destroy Iran’s limited and exposed oil fleet.”

Earlier, Iranian state TV said four US missiles struck a tanker about six miles from Kharg Island, where there is a terminal through which the country exports most of its oil.



Kharg Island has been repeatedly targeted during the war, including US strikes on military sites there in March.

The strikes came nearly a week after the US and Iran resumed attacks following a month of relative calm.

As tensions flare, US President Donald Trump declared he may strike Iran’s Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site.

The US president also described the spiralling war with Tehran as “small potatoes for us”.

Iran’s nuclear program, the issue that sparked the war in February, was meant to be addressed in negotiations that fell apart soon after the US and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding in mid-June.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Instead, Tehran’s new leverage focuses on the Strait of Hormuz – a crucial waterway used to transport oil and natural gas.

The US military has been helping guide ships through the strait as Tehran continues to assert its control and targets vessels.

News.title: Murder probe as man in his 30s found dead with serious head injuries in south London
News.content:
DEATH MYSTERY Murder probe as man in his 30s found dead with serious head injuries in south London

A MURDER investigation has been launched after a man was found dead with serious head injuries.

Police were called to an address in Lambeth, south London, at around 8.30am on Friday by the London Fire Brigade.

Officers found a man in his 30s with serious head injuries and he was pronounced dead at the scene.

No arrests have been made at this stage and a crime scene remains in place.





The Metropolitan Police have urged anyone with information to contact the force.

Detective chief inspector Alison Foxwell said: “This is a tragic incident and our thoughts are with the victim’s family and loved ones as they come to terms with their loss.

“We are working hard to establish exactly what happened and a team of detectives is progressing a number of enquiries at pace.

“At this stage, we believe this was an isolated incident and there is no evidence to suggest any wider risk to the public.

“I would urge anyone who was in the area, or who may have seen or heard anything unusual, to come forward and speak to us.

“Even the smallest piece of information could prove vital in helping us understand the circumstances surrounding this man’s death.

“We understand this news will cause concern within the local community and residents can expect to see an increased police presence in the area as our investigation continues.”

A spokesperson for the police said: “At around 20:35hrs on Friday, 4 September, officers were called by the London Fire Brigade to an address in Poynders Road, SW4.



“Police attended alongside the London Ambulance Service and found a man in his 30s suffering from serious head injuries. Despite the efforts of emergency services, he was sadly pronounced dead at the scene.

“His next of kin have been informed and are being supported by specialist officers.”

News.title: ‘Idiot’ camper pitches tent on edge of crumbling 150ft cliff at beauty spot made famous by hit TV show
News.content:
CLIFF HANGER ‘Idiot’ camper pitches tent on edge of crumbling 150ft cliff at beauty spot made famous by hit TV show

A THOUGHTLESS camper pitched a tent on the edge of a 150ft crumbling cliff.

Locals were shocked when the spot the campsite erected just a few feet from the rockfall-prone cliff in West Bay, Doreset.



The beauty spot was made famous in ITV crime drama Broadchurch.

The camper, a lone man in a t-shirt and shorts, scaled a fence placed by the council to stop walkers going near the cliff edge.



The man would have also ignored the numerous “warning” signs to reach the spot.

Nine rockfalls were recorded last year alone, with a huge pile of debris below the cliffs from previous landslips.



In January, a catastrophic collapse sent 500 tonnes of rock crashing down onto the beach below.

Boulders the size of small cars smashed into the sand, unleashing a suffocating dust cloud into the sky.



But despite the threat of a fatal plunge, the camper seemingly slept above a huge crack in the 180-million year-old sandstone which could give way at anytime.

A witness said: “That’s what you call living life on the edge.

“They clearly decided it was the perfect vantage point to watch the sunset before going to sleep for the night.”



The camper also faced the risk of being hit by a stray golf ball as he positioned himself to the side of the green of the 15th hole at Bridport and West Dorset Golf Club.

The camper was spotted at 8pm last night by photographer Graham Hunt who could not believe what he was seeing.

He said: “I don’t know what goes through people’s minds but I suppose they are thinking ‘I’m going to sleep here because I have the best view of the sunset’.

“The footpath has been closed for two and a half years by the council because they believe it is unsafe.

“He had to jump over a fence and ignore clear warning signs to get there.



“It does seem rather idiotic.”

In 2012 tourist Charlotte Blackman, 22, was crushed to death by a huge landslip as she walked under the cliffs further along the World Heritage Site at Burton Bradstock.

A Dorset Council spokesperson said: “The Jurassic Coast looks the way it does because of erosion – meaning it is always on the move.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“It is a wonderful place to visit, but it’s important to use common sense and caution – stay away from the edge and base of cliffs and always pay attention to warning signs and safety messages.”

The Dorset beauty spot has been popular among tourists this summer, with thousands of sunseekers flocking to the country’s coastlines.

News.title: Brit mum, 45, held in jail in Egypt on ‘bogus charges over sister’s videos’ – as desperate husband begs UK to intervene
News.content:
MUM CAGED Brit mum, 45, held in jail in Egypt on ‘bogus charges over sister’s videos’ – as desperate husband begs UK to intervene

A BRIT mum – of -four has been jailed in Egypt allegedly on made-up charges.

Eman el-Shazly’s family fears she has been taken in a bid to add pressure to her activist sister.



Eman el-Shazly, 45, from Birmingham was allegedly taken from her mother’s home in Cairo in the early hours of August 17.

Her husband Zeesharn Moustapha said the arrest came just one day after authorities “ram-raided” the property and told her “you need to tell your sister to stop”.



Mum-of-four Eman had called him screaming “they’re coming to get me” – and the next day she was imprisoned in the 10th Ramadan Rehabilitation Centre.

Eman had been visiting Egypt to care for her sick 68-year-old mother – who already has two children in detention.

After more than two weeks locked up on “bogus charges”, her husband said that Eman’s mother and two nieces were allowed to visit her for the first time.

Describing the heartbreaking visit, he said: “They only saw them for 15 minutes.

“For the first five to eight minutes, the officers who were there were just swearing at the family, pushing and shoving.

In reference to the videos by Eman’s sister criticising the Egyptian government, the guards taunted: “Is your sister going to stop now? Is she going to stop now?”



“They were laughing at them, pushing them and shoving them physically. They just sat there in fear.”

He added that the family brought enough food to feed 30 women locked inside the cells because he believes the government do not feed inmates enough.

Zeesharn said his wife’s mother was left “in pieces” after seeing her daughter, describing her as a “broken person”.



Fearful of being arrested upon landing, Zeesharn has not yet visited Egypt himself.

“With this problem now, it looks like I won’t be going to Egypt again”, he said.

“It’s just devastation. People are heartbroken”, he added.

His wife Eman will remain behind bars at least until her trial on September 13.

Egyptian authorities accuse her of promoting terrorism and spreading false news on her social media accounts.



Defending Eman, lawyer Arfan Rashid said he did not know which posts the government was referring to and that they had no evidence that she had personally promoted a terrorist organisation.

Rashid believes the charges are based on the activity of Eman’s sister in the UK.

Slamming the arrest, Zeesharn has called it “illegal collective punishment” – and has previously said the UK government response has been “lacklustre at best”.



He has told the UK government to “get their head out of their a***s” and intervene in the case of his imprisoned wife.

He said: “We’re waiting for the Government to do something about it, or try to at least make a public comment.

“This is where we need the UK Government and human-rights organisations.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We need these big people involved.”

A spokesperson for the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) said: “We are supporting the family of a British national detained in Egypt, and are in contact with the authorities.”

News.title: Manhunt for ‘flasher’ wearing fishnets who exposed himself to two dog walkers in ‘distressing’ incidents in seaside town
News.content:
FLASHER HORROR Manhunt for ‘flasher’ wearing fishnets who exposed himself to two dog walkers in ‘distressing’ incidents in seaside town

COPS have launched a manhunt for a flasher after a man allegedly exposed himself to two dog walkers in a seaside town.

The suspect is said to have been wearing a short skirt and fishnets during the horror in Bournemouth, Dorset, on Wednesday morning.

Both dog walkers had been strolling through Granby Road when they came across the flasher.

The first woman reportedly spotted the man indecently exposing himself at around 7am.





It is understood the same man was seen flashing again by another woman an hour later, Dorset Police said.

The force has urged witnesses or anyone with information on the “distressing” incidents to come forward.

According to eyewitness reports, the man was white and of a slim build.

He was reportedly wearing a short denim skirt, fishnets and dark jacket at the time of the alleged exposures.

PC Jamie Spry said: “This was distressing for both of the victims and we are carrying out enquiries to identify the person involved.

“I am keen to hear from anyone with information that might assist our investigation or who saw a man matching the description given in the area on the morning of Wednesday 2 September 2026.”

It comes just days after a man was arrested following an alleged indecent exposure and assault involving a woman and a child.

The 41-year-old man was detained after the incident in Leeds on Sunday and he remains in custody.



The incident occurred at around 7.30pm near on York Road in the Killingbeck area.

The woman and child were reportedly in a car and are currently being supported by specialist officers.

News.title: Eerie pictures of playground Patrick Clancy opened in honor of 3 dead children lying silent during Lindsay’s trial
News.content:
EERIE pictures have revealed the playground that Patrick Clancy opened to honor his three dead children lying empty just before a mistrial was declared on Friday.

The former husband of Lindsay Clancy opened the Clancy Family Playground at Wadsworth Field Park in Duxbury, Massachusetts, in June 2025.



It was built by volunteers to honor the lives of his three children with Lindsay – 5-year-old Cora, 3-year-old Dawson, and 8-month-old Callan Clancy.

Patrick cut a ribbon to open the park on June 7, 2025, and local children were invited to play at the park and remember his children who called Duxbury home.



The project was organized by the HEARD Foundation, which was founded by Patrick to support parental mental health.

Lindsay went on trial in July 2026 for killing her three children in their Massachusetts home in January 2023.



The jury heard prosecutors claim Lindsay strangled each of the children with exercise bands in the basement of their home.

The former delivery nurse then cut herself with a knife on her wrists and neck, before jumping out of a bedroom window, leaving her paralyzed from the waist down.

She has admitted to the killings, but her defense argued she was suffering from severe postpartum psychosis and say that she was therefore not legally responsible.

Prosecutors argued that she deliberately planned the killings and understood that they were wrong.



For five weeks, jurors in Plymouth, Massachusetts, were confronted with one of the most heart-wrenching criminal cases in the US.

On September 4, one juror out of 12 held out and refused to be persuaded by the other 11, which sparked a mistrial.

What happens next in the Clancy case? Now that a mistrial has been declared, the jury has been discharged. This means that there is no guilty or not guilty verdict, the trial is incomplete, and the legal proceedings have been reset to their pre-trial state. Since Clancy has been neither convicted or acquitted, the Double Jeopardy clause – which prevents someone from being tried twice for the same crime – does not apply. In most cases of mistrial through jury deadlock, it allows the prosecution to try Clancy again with a whole new jury. Prosecutors do not need to file new or amended charges as the original indictment remains active. All bail orders before the trial have remained in place and the matter has been adjourned until September 29. Clancy will remain in the same mental health facility she has been held in for the entire trial.

Patrick, who only appeared at court to take the stand, was pictured by The U.S. Sun earlier this week with his new wife.

His lawyer issued a statement, stressing that he was already dreading a retrial.

“The loss of Patrick’s children is something from which he will never recover and from which there will never be closure,” it read. “The prospect of reliving this tragedy through another trial is extraordinarily painful — for Patrick, for his family, and for all us.”



Lindsay showed little emotion on September 4 after the judge declared a mistrial.



It means the jury was unable to reach a unanimous verdict and she was neither convicted nor acquitted. Prosecutors could seek to retry the case.

The jury had been deadlocked since Tuesday.

The court is scheduled to reconvene on September 29 to discuss the next steps in the legal proceedings.
