If you or someone you know is affected by any of the issues raised in this story, call or text the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988, chat on 988lifeline.org, or text Crisis Text Line at 741741.

News.title: UK to bask in 28C heat tomorrow with ‘very warm’ day before Met Office warns of rain, gales and ‘cool nights’
News.content:
LAST DAY OF SUMMER? UK to bask in 28C heat tomorrow with ‘very warm’ day before Met Office warns of rain, gales and ‘cool nights’

BRITS are set for a final warm spell as temperatures of 28C are forecast before rain and gales move in.

Sunshine is expected for most of the country tomorrow as the UK has a final glimpse of summer sun.



Edinburgh and Belfast will hit 21C, while Manchester and Cardiff will reach the mid 20s but London is forecast to be the warmest at 28C.

The Met Office spokesperson said: “A brief warmer spell to come and then temperatures fall back to average next week.”



By next week temperatures will fall back to the high teens for most of England and the mid 20s in London.

A few showers are forecast for the rest of today in the north of England but the rest of the country will be basking in warm sunshine.



A dry night is expected for eastern and southeastern England with a slight breeze.

The northwest will see a stronger breeze and even some pockets of rain.



Sunday morning will start with an overcast sky and showers for most, but the rain will stick to the north and far west later in the day.

In the south and southeast, Brits can expect very warm sunshine.

Scotland and Ireland will see highs of 15-20C which despite not hitting the highs elsewhere is still several degrees above average for the time of year.

At the start of next week the rain will move across the rest of the country.

This is due to fresh Atlantic air and rain bands arriving next week.



The Met Office said Tuesday will bring a mix of sunshine and showers with heavy rain in the north and a possibility of strong winds.

Temperatures are set to fall back down to average after this weekend’s highs.

Looking ahead, the rest of the month is set to be dry with colder nights and the occasional outbreak of rain.

The warmer start to September comes after Environment Secretary Dame Angela Eagle warned Brits to stock up on food ahead of extreme weather.

She said that the El Nino developing over the pacific ocean will lead to “more extreme storms in this country“.



Speaking to The Guardian Dame Angela added: “If you’ve got a store of a bit of food that can keep you going for a while before the emergency services can get to you, you’re going to be a lot better off than if you haven’t.

“So some of it is that kind of preparation for just being a bit more resilient.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Her comments follow a warning from the National Audit Office that Britain is less prepared for an emergency than other countries such as Sweden and Finland.

News.title: Reform UK conference LIVE: Empty seats for Nigel Farage's closing speech after crisis-hit event
News.content:
Reform UK's conference descended into chaos after Scotland Yard said it was assessing reports that senior figures sought to evade electoral law over donations

Reform UK's chaotic and underwhelming conference will finally come to an end shortly - in what will likely be relief for Nigel Farage.

The Reform UK leader - who lost two of his top aides during the three-day gathering - is giving a closing speech to delegates at Birmingham's National Exhibition Centre. He has been battling to get his crisis-hit party back on track after a donations scandal overshadowed the conference.

His keynote speech on the main stage yesterday was beset by chaos after he was interrupted by multiple hecklers. Security teams dragged out protestors as disorder ripped through the conference.

And Tory defector Robert Jenrick lost his cool this morning after being asked about the allegations facing Reform. The rattled Reform Treasury spokesman accused a TV presenter of wanting to “waste the interview talking about tittle tattle” and dismissed the undercover sting - that forced two Reform aides to step down - as a report by “some pranksters".

Reform faces the possibility of investigations by the police and the Electoral Commission into the report by Channel 4 News and Verbatim Investigations.

Mr Farage has tried to downplay the secretly-recorded comments as "loose pub talk" and said Reform won’t be distracted by a "campaign of attacks". He insisted Reform has “broken no laws” and had not “taken any dodgy money”.

News.title: Dover protest - live: Hundreds of masked men stop access to port as MP says 'get a job'
News.content:
Hundreds of masked protesters blocked access to the Port of Dover and the A20 approach road, causing major disruption for people travelling by ferry

Dover protest - live: Hundreds of masked men stop access to port as MP says 'get a job'

Hundreds of masked "stop the boats" protesters dressed in black blocked access to the Port of Dover, causing chaos for holidaymakers and lorry drivers, with one motorist saying he "feared for his life".

Demonstrators blocked key approach roads to the port, including the A20 and A2, for around three hours today (Saturday). They also spray-painted the words "blood is on your hands" on the ground outside a migrant processing facility. The Government condemned the protesters' behaviour and the disruption caused to travellers.

One motorist, Toby Mackenzie, said in a post on social media: "People dressed in black surrounding my car, pretty much left me fearing for my life."

Mike Tapp, Labour MP for Dover and Deal, branded the protesters "idiots", telling them to "go home, enjoy your weekend/get a job". "I bet if you asked any one of those 'protesters' they wouldn’t know small boat crossing are down by 40%," he added.

P&O Ferries warned that access to the port was restricted and that anyone who missed their ferry would be able to board the next available service.

News.title: Ukraine 'ready' for limited ceasefire as Moscow and US officials begin negotiations
News.content:
Ukraine 'ready' for limited ceasefire as Moscow and US officials begin negotiations

The Ukrainian president said he had spoken with Donald Trump's team and that US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner were preparing for diplomatic engagements with Ukrainian officials.

View 4 Images (Image: Ukrinform/Shutterstock)

Ukraine is ready to observe a limited ceasefire in airstrikes on Kyiv and Moscow as US officials begin negotiations with Russia over a potential end to the war, has said.

‌



The Ukrainian president said he had spoken with Donald Trump's team and that US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner were preparing for diplomatic engagements with Ukrainian officials.

‌



Zelenskyy said the discussions marked the point at which Ukraine was prepared to halt strikes on Moscow while negotiations were under way, with Kyiv expecting Russia to take the same approach.

‌



"From now through the end of Saturday, as well as on Sunday and Monday, Ukraine is ready to refrain from strikes on Moscow, and we expect the Russians to do the same regarding Kyiv," he said.

View 4 Images (Image: AP Photo/Francisco Seco)

Earlier on Saturday, Russian state officials confirmed that Vladimir Putin had ordered a 72-hour pause in attacks on Kyiv.

‌



Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov told Russian state news agency Tass that Russian forces would stop strikes on the Ukrainian capital for three days from midnight on Saturday.

"Putin has ordered that no strikes be carried out against Kyiv for three days, starting at midnight today (Saturday)," Peskov said.

He said the decision was linked to preparations for the arrival of US envoys Witkoff and Kushner, who are due to hold talks with Ukrainian officials as Washington continues efforts to broker a peace deal.

‌



The pair landed in Moscow on Saturday ahead of the weekend's diplomatic discussions. Trump told reporters on Friday that the envoys were "bringing with them a proposal to end the war".

Their visit comes after months of stalled attempts by the US and its allies to bring an end to the conflict, which has now entered its fifth year.

The US delegation was met at the airport by Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev, according to Tass. Dmitriev shared photographs of himself meeting the officials as they arrived, alongside the caption: "Welcome to Moscow Peacemakers."

‌



View 4 Images (Image: SERGEY BOBYLEV/SPUTNIK/KREMLIN/POOL/EPA/Shutterstock)

Witkoff and Kushner last visited Moscow in January, when they met Putin at the Kremlin. They have not previously visited Kyiv, but Zelenskyy said he was expecting them in the Ukrainian capital on Sunday.

He said plans for diplomatic engagements with US officials in Kyiv had been approved.

‌



"We are waiting for Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and are ready for a substantive conversation," Zelenskyy said.

The proposed pause comes amid an escalation in aerial attacks by both sides.

Russia has intensified its bombardment of Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities in recent weeks, with attacks increasingly stretching into daylight hours. The strikes have put further pressure on Ukraine's air defence capabilities.

‌



View 4 Images (Image: X / @kadmitriev/AFP via Getty Images)

On Friday, a Russian drone struck the headquarters of Ukraine's Security Service, known as the SBU, in Kyiv.

The agency is among those involved in carrying out long-range operations inside Russia.

Article continues below

Ukraine has also stepped up long-range attacks on Russian territory, targeting military facilities, oil refineries and other infrastructure in an effort to disrupt Moscow's war effort and put pressure on the Russian economy.

The latest diplomatic push comes as Washington's efforts to secure a wider peace agreement have lost momentum, with US attention also focused in recent months on its conflict with Iran.

The 72-hour pause ordered by Putin, alongside Ukraine's offer to refrain from strikes on Moscow, could provide a limited window for the US-backed talks to take place without further escalation from either side.

News.title: Inside Patrick Clancy's new life and fresh start in New York after wife Lindsay killed kids
News.content:
Inside Patrick Clancy's new life and fresh start in New York after wife Lindsay killed kids

After losing Cora, Dawson and Callan stepped away from work, took up sailing, ran the Boston Marathon and lather launched a charity in their names

View 5 Images Patrick went on to marry New York fertility doctor Dr Rachel Danis in 2026 (Image: David L. Ryan/Pool The Boston Gl)

Patrick Clancy has quietly rebuilt his life in New York after losing his three young children in a tragedy which shattered his family.

‌



Just four months after Cora, five, Dawson, three, and eight-month-old Callan were killed by their mother Lindsay Clancy, Patrick left Massachusetts and moved into an apartment in Manhattan.

‌



More than three years on, he has remarried and thrown himself into charity work honouring his children - but reminders of the life he lost have remained close.

‌



When The New Yorker visited his apartment in 2024, Patrick had kept treasured belongings from Cora, Dawson and Callan around his new home. A toy helicopter Dawson received for his final Christmas remained among his possessions, while cushions had been made from pieces of the children’s clothes. A pink blanket covered in rainbows was kept on his sofa.

Patrick admitted that even after their deaths, he would sometimes catch himself saying: “I have three kids,” before adding, “They are deceased.”

View 5 Images A mistrial was recently declared after jurors failed to reach a verdict (Image: Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images)

‌



Lindsay Clancy mistrial declared after jury deadlocks over deaths of her three children READ MORE :

Meghan Markle may not appear in public for weeks after moving back to UK with Prince Harry READ MORE :

A new life in New York

In the months after his children’s deaths, Patrick took an extended break from his job at Microsoft, according to The New Yorker, before slowly beginning to find new routines.

He joined a sailing club and started training for the Boston Marathon, completing the race in April 2024 in memory of all three children while raising money for Boston Children’s Hospital.

Patrick also filed for divorce from Lindsay in February 2024. He went on to marry New York fertility doctor Dr Rachel Danis in 2026, according to People.

‌



View 5 Images Patrick Clancy pictured with his wife Rachel Danis at the NYC Marathon (Image: Instagram)

But while his life has moved forward, Patrick has repeatedly spoken about Lindsay before the killings and his belief that her mental health had dramatically deteriorated.

“I wasn’t married to a monster,” Patrick said. “I was married to someone who got sick.”

‌



A legacy for his three children

Patrick has also tried to turn some of his grief into work aimed at helping other families. In 2024, he launched The Heard Foundation with his sisters Erin and Laura in memory of Cora, Dawson and Callan.

“Born from profound loss and bound by love, the Heard Foundation was founded in memory of Cora, Dawson, and Callan Clancy,” reads the charity’s website.

The organisation aims to “reimagine perinatal mental-health care” and ultimately “build a dedicated treatment center where parents can heal with dignity and support,” while working to “foster a culture of kindness and connection so no one struggles alone,” according to its website.

‌



View 5 Images He launched The Heard Foundation in memory of Cora, Dawson and Callan (Image: GoFundMe)

Courtroom drama

But the tragedy which forced Patrick to rebuild his life remains unresolved in court.

Patrick had returned to his family’s home in Duxbury, Massachusetts, on January 24, 2023, to discover his three children had been strangled. Cora and Dawson died that night, while Callan was taken to a hospital and died days later.

‌



Lindsay, a former labour and delivery nurse, does not deny killing Cora, Dawson and Callan, but pleaded not guilty by reason of lack of criminal responsibility.

Her lawyers argued she had been suffering from postpartum psychosis, while prosecutors maintained she knew what she was doing and that the killings were intentional. On Friday, following a five-week trial and says of deliberations, audible gasp was heard in the courtroom as Judge William F. Sullivan said he was going to declare a mistrial.

But just as the jurors were about to come back to the courtroom, Lindsay Clancy's lawyer asked to make a last-minute request for a higher court to stave off the mistrial. That kicked off a tense wait while a judge on the state's top court considered the ask.

‌



The whiplash moment was one last piece of courtroom drama in a livestreamed trial that captivated and divided many. And now prosecutors must decide whether to do it all over again with a second trial.

View 5 Images Patrick faces the prospect of another trial (Image: Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images)

Patrick, who testified during the proceedings in July, said through his lawyer David Meier that the possibility of having to go through another trial would bring further anguish.

Article continues below

Meier's statement reads: “Patrick Clancy is grateful to the Court and to the jurors for their hard work, their commitment, and their perseverance. The loss of Patrick’s children is something from which he will never recover and from which there will never be closure. The prospect of reliving this tragedy through another trial is extraordinarily painful - for Patrick, for his family, and for all of us.”

More than three years after the tragedy, Patrick continues to rebuild his life in New York while honouring Cora, Dawson and Callan in the years since their deaths.

News.title: Pollsters say by-election in Keir Starmer's old seat could be 'make or break' for Zack Polanski
News.content:
Pollsters say by-election in Keir Starmer's old seat could be 'make or break' for Zack Polanski

EXCLUSIVE: Pollsters explained Labour were still the favourites for the Holborn and St Pancras seat, and that the 'shine' had come off Zack Polanski with voters

View 2 Images The by-election could be make or break for Zack Polanski (Image: TOLGA AKMEN/EPA/Shutterstock)

The bombshell by-election in Keir Starmer’s old seat could be “make or break” for the Green leader Zack Polanski, polling experts have claimed.

‌



The former PM announced he was standing down this week, just months after leaving Downing Street.

‌



Speaking to this newspaper, pollsters explained Labour were still the favourites for the Holborn and St Pancras seat, and that the “shine” had come off Mr Polanski with voters.

‌



Polling guru Sir John Curtice said: “Polanski obviously made quite a name for himself, but his personal popularity isn’t quite what it was, and hasn’t been since the Golders Green incident. This looks at least as tough a gig for Polanski, if he stands, as Makerfield looked for Burnham.

“The difference is that Burnham could always hope to and did succeed in persuading people who might otherwise vote Green, Lib Dem or even Tory to vote Labour to keep Reform out. Those kind of dynamics are not really available to Polanski as he’s the extremist in this instance, rather than the person in the centre.

View 2 Images Professor Sir John Curtice said Labour were the favourites for the seat (Image: Getty Images)

‌



“It will be a real test to use his personal popularity to defy the odds. Polanski’s chances are greater than zero, but he will be taking on a quite considerable challenge. It might be make or break for him in terms of his political future”.

The Green Party leader had been forced to apologise after sharing a post on social media questioning the actions of police in the Golders Green attack. The officers had kicked a man in the head after he'd stabbed two Jewish men in a horrifying terror attack.

Pollster Luke Tryl also labelled Labour favourites, and suggested Mr Polanski would have had a much greater chance if Mr Starmer was still in Downing Street.

‌



He said: “If this election were in May I think I would say the Greens might have had a really good chance at taking the seat.

“Since then, Andy Burnham has re-engaged a group of disillusioned progressives, the Burnham bounce largely comes from voters on the left.

“Also Zack Polanski has had some personal missteps, including Golders Green, his response to that, but also council tax. He's just taking a bit of a shine off, and you've seen a dip in the polling.

Article continues below

“Labour start off as favourites, but we have seen when party leaders stand themselves in by-election contests, the candidate really matters.

“Makerfield should have been an easy Reform win but it wasn’t because of Andy Burnham.”

Labour has won the inner London constituency since it was created in 1983, winning at least 40% of the vote at every election.

News.title: UK's El Nino problem as Brits set for extreme winter and food shortages possible
News.content:
UK's El Nino problem as Brits set for extreme winter and food shortages possible

Environment Secretary Angela Eagle has warned households to stock up on food to prepare for extreme weather in the UK as experts warn that this El Niño event could be the strongest since at least 1950

View 5 Images The Met Office says El Nino could bring stormy weather to the UK in Autumn and early Winter (Image: PA)

The Met Office says El Nino is set to make the UK's autumn and early winter particularly wet and stormy - as the weather system also threatens to hit the nation's food supplies.

‌



El Niño, a weather phenomenon that develops in the Pacific Ocean, is "firmly established" and will strengthen into a "very strong event" in the coming months, impacting rainfall and temperature patterns across the world and fuelling extreme weather, according to the World Meteorological Organization (WMO).

‌



The Met Office says it expects this El Nino to "increase the chances of wetter, stormier conditions for North West Europe, including the UK, in the coming autumn and early winter".

‌



And Environment Secretary Angela Eagle has urged UK households to stock up on food in preparation for the weather system causing "more extreme storms in this country".

View 5 Images El Nino is set to bring stormy weather to the UK - increasing the risk of flooding (Image: PA)

UK weather maps show 3C chill as Brits face shock cold snap in weeks READ MORE :

Meanwhile, the extreme weather may also put pressure on global food supply, including the UK's. Analysis from the Energy and Climate Unit (ECIU) found that countries that could be exposed to climate extremes were the source of 13 per cent of UK food imports.

‌



That means food such as rice, for which India is the UKs biggest supplier and citrus fruits from South Africa and Peru, coffee from Brazil and tea from Kenya could all be impacted.

View 5 Images Angela Eagle said Brits need to be better prepared for potential climate-related emergencies (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Dame Angela said: "We're about to experience probably the largest El Niño that has ever been seen, and that will lead to drier summers, wetter winters, with more extreme storms in this country.

‌



"It will do a lot more damage in Asia with flooding, and therefore I think that we need to take it seriously. If you've got a store of a bit of food that can keep you going for a while before the emergency services can get to you, you're going to be a lot better off than if you haven't. So some of it is that kind of preparation for just being a bit more resilient."

View 5 Images Rescuers evacuate residents trapped by flooding triggered by Typhoon Saudel in Fuzhou, China's Fujian province (Image: China News Service via Getty Images)

The regions most likely to bear the brunt of El Niño are North and South America, Central America, Africa, the Euro-Asian continent and Australia, the European Commission said in June.

‌



The World Food Programme said in August that the El Niño was likely to push almost 50 million people into acute hunger, with those in countries in Central America and southern Africa expected to be the hardest hit.

Sea surface temperatures across the central-eastern equatorial Pacific - the region at the heart of El Niño - are already well above average and are continuing to rise, WMO said.

The widely used Niño 3.4 index show sea surface temperatures temperatures between late July and mid-August were between 2.2C and 2.6C above average.

‌



View 5 Images El Nino can cause extreme rainfall as well drought across the globe - this map shows precipitation (Image: World Meteorological Organization (WMO))

El Niño is forecast to peak in November, when monthly sea surface temperatures reaching could reach around 4C, according to the average of 14 different models. This would make it the strongest event since at least 1950.

Research shows that global heating is intensifying El Niño cycles, which in turn worsens the impacts of the climate crisis.

Article continues below

UN Secretary-General António Guterres said: "El Niño is being supersized before our eyes. The science leaves no room for doubt: the planet is in uncharted waters, and those waters are heating up.

"The world is in the danger zone of extreme weather. The race now is between rising risks and our commitment to take climate action and protect people. We must win that race."

News.title: Reform conference sees woman hit on head with crutch and hair pulled in sickening clip
News.content:
Reform conference sees woman hit on head with crutch and hair pulled in sickening clip

West Midlands Police says it is looking at footage showing a woman being hit with a crutch after she interrupted Nigel Farage's conference speech, with Nadine Dorries saying it was 'shocking' there were protesters there

View 3 Images Police are examining footage of a woman being assaulted at Reform's conference (Image: X)

A senior Reform figure has said people who heckle Nigel Farage will not get “gentle treatment” - while police examine footage of a woman being assaulted by members.

‌



A sickening clip shows a woman being hit around the head with a crutch before her hair is pulled and a hand put over her mouth at the party conference. The grey haired man seen assaulting her was not a member of the event's security team.

‌



Another woman from the crowd can be seen pulling the protester's hair as guards escorted her from Birmingham's NEC. Asked by The Mirror whether those involved should face consequences during a debate about free speech, Nadine Dorries said those who disrupt speakers should not expect to be treated gently and said it was "shocking" that protesters had been there.

‌



Ms Dorries, who was Tory Culture Secretary under Boris Johnson before defecting to Reform, said: “Somebody said to me it was shocking to see protesters being treated the way they were. I think what was also shocking was the way they thought they could come into the conference and try to derail Nigel Farage’s speech.”

Content cannot be displayed without consent

And she went on: “If you’re going to come into a conference like this… of course you’re not going to get gentle treatment.” And she added: “It’s wrong, no one should be punched." She went on: "No one should attend this conference and try and disrupt it.”

‌



Her remarks came after The Mirror asked if those who assaulted protesters should face consequences. Reform's home affairs spokesman, Zia Yusuf, responded: “To the question from The Mirror about whether I condemn people punching people, yes I do condemn people punching people.”

Mr Farage was interrupted four times during his keynote speech at the right-wing shindig in Birmingham. He laughed as the first demonstrator was taken away and Reform fans chanted "out, out, out".

Reform's chairman used his speech to make a joke about the incident. Lee Anderson told delegates: "A few nuisances we had in the hall yesterday, the protesters...

‌



"I did see an old chap, a pensioner, somewhere with a walking stick... Look I don't condone any of that type of behaviour, but if anyone wants to have a quick whip around later we are collecting for a new walking stick.

View 3 Images Nadine Dorries said it was 'shocking' that protesters heckled Nigel Farage (Image: ITV)

"He's in here somewhere." It is understood that all those removed were from a group called Climate Resistance, and had joined Reform in order to buy tickets.

‌



The group responded on Instagram: "Is this the beaviour you expect from the party that says it wants to govern Britain?" West Midlands Police said it is aware of the footage and called on the woman to come forward.

A spokesman told The Mirror: “We’re aware of a video circulating from the Reform UK Conference showing an incident with a protester.

“We haven’t received a complaint but would ask the woman involved to come forward and contact us so we can carry out enquiries. Anyone with any information should contact us on 101 quoting log number 924 of 5 September.”

‌



As she was being led away, another demonstrator told The Mirror she was protesting about Mr Farage taking cash from billionaires. Asked why she had interrupted, she said: "Nigel Farage taking money from billionaires, which has been exposed multiple times. Taking money from billionaires, including Christopher Harborne, the crypto billionaire."

View 3 Images The hecklers interrupted Nigel Farage's speech on Friday (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Another group member who was thrown out, named Ed, told this newspaper: "We just stood up in the Reform conference to highlight the corruption at the heart of the Reform Party."

‌



Asked what he shouted at Mr Farage, he said: "There was quite a lot of adrenaline in the moment, so I think what I shouted was roughly, 'Are you one of these people who's corrupted by donations, Nigel?'"

Ed went on: "So the idea was to raise people's awareness of that and to show that that's happening, because they talk a lot about nation and community values in that room. And I believe some of the people there are genuinely there because that's what they believe, but they should know that this is a party that will flout the rules to get into power, and that just doesn't really care about the kinds of things that would keep us as ordinary citizens that we would actually have to obey."

And he continued: "I hope that we've raised awareness of the corruption scandal that is just blowing up today, because this is something that hopefully will make people aware that Reform is not a party that can be trusted in power."

News.title: Greek F-4 fighter jet crashes and 'explodes' in front of horrified crowd at airshow
News.content:
Greek F-4 fighter jet crashes and 'explodes' in front of horrified crowd at airshow

A Greek F-4 Phantom fighter jet crashed during an air show at Tanagra Air Base, near Athens, on Saturday afternoon

View Image The two-seat F-4 Phantom aircraft was seen losing altitude several minutes before the crash

A Greek F-4 Phantom fighter jet has crashed in front of thousands of spectators during an air show near Athens.

‌



The crash happened at Tanagra Air Base shortly before 3pm local time (1pm BST) on Saturday during the Athens Flying Week air show, according to Greek public broadcaster ERT.

‌



ERT reported that an explosion occurred immediately after the crash. The two-seat aircraft was seen losing altitude and descending towards the ground several minutes before the crash, which took place in front of thousands of people, the broadcaster said.

Article continues below

Video footage showed a column of black smoke rising into the sky a few hundred metres from spectators at the event. A firefighting helicopter circled above the crash site, where crews worked to contain two separate fires.

It is not yet known whether the two pilots managed to eject before the crash. There were no immediate reports of injuries among spectators.

News.title: Disruption at Port of Dover as masked 'stop the boats' protesters block roads
News.content:
There has been major disruption at the Port of Dover due to a large group of masked men holding a demonstration.

Hundreds of protesters, dressed in black and wearing face coverings, blocked roads and were heard chanting "stop the boats".

Traffic was stopped from going in and out of the port, with the government saying it condemned "the behaviour in Dover and the travel disruption it has caused".

Kent Police, which made no arrests, described it as a "spontaneous" protest. Officers moved the crowd from the port to Dover Priory railway station at about 11:30 BST and the force said "all involved had dispersed by 12:00".

Paul King, Reform UK councillor for Dover West, said he had been told it was a "stop the boats protest".

Kent Police has not yet commented on who was behind the demo.

Far-right activists Tommy Robinson and Danny Thomas both posted about it on X, praising those involved.

Thomas is believed to be the founder of the Patriot Platform network.

Anti-hate organisation Hope Not Hate claims that Patriot Platform arranged the protest, saying the group began meeting in July and has brought together members of anti-migrant groups from around the country.

Demonstrators told the BBC they did not want to talk to the media, although one said "send them back" and another said "stop the boats" when approached.

News.title: Nigel Farage tells BBC he 'wasn't listening' during foreign donor talks filmed undercover
News.content:
There's no question the allegations in the Channel 4 film have been embarrassing for Reform, and disrupted what they hoped would be a conference about their plans for office if they win the next General Election.

Everywhere around the huge, draughty exhibition hall in Birmingham are giant posters and placards saying, "Reform - the first 100 days".

They wanted to herald their deal with a serious contender to be the next French President, Jordan Bardella, to deal with small boats.

They were keen to highlight the promise to cut income tax if they win the election, scheduled to be in 2029.

They wanted to talk about their proposals for education, welfare, planning, and the rest.

Party members, delighted to have a reason to get together, have taken part in those sessions, applauded and cheered in the hall; gone wild for Farage on stage.

But for the rest of the country, most of the noise from the conference will have been the huge and awkward story about the toxic mix of politics and money.

What is harder to assess is the impact this mess will have on Farage's standing with the public, after a tricky summer and a recent poll slump.

At the top of the party there is a quiet admission that what has happened here is a genuine mistake.

One senior figure told me they could brush off other claims of murky funding, confident nothing had gone wrong - but they conceded these claims do matter, and that for a certain vital percentage of voters, it would "cause them to ask questions".

No one is pretending it's just what Farage tried to joke was a "little, local difficulty".

And there is a private acknowledgement that stories like this can be off putting to voters beyond Reform's no doubt very enthusiastic base.

Another party source told me they were "totally blindsided" by the revelations; stunned "there'd just been no diligence" and in disbelief at how Jukes and Orr, who both say they'd done nothing wrong, seem to have behaved.

A different member of the party's top team said, "hopefully, it's just growing pains". In other words, Reform's developed so fast that sometimes mistakes are made. But they told me: "The party has to step up â sometimes the people that got us here, aren't the people for the next stage".

Among Farage's fans at the conference, I found different views. One member was convinced the party is treated unfairly: "It's the blob, it's all against him," she said.

But another young Reform enthusiast rejected that, telling me: "It's all documented and there on camera â Nigel has to be more careful about what party members say."

But there is a sense of "here we go again". When I asked another member what they thought of the financial scandal, a weary answer, "Which one?"

This time last year in the same conference complex, Reform felt like they were simply sweeping all before them. Twelve months on, they are having to work harder, the scrutiny is more intense, and the pressure only growing.

Farage's claim that he "wasn't listening" to the conversation was telling â to get to power without more of these kinds of serious embarrassments, he may have to pay more attention to what is going on.

News.title: Chris Mason: Reform UK winded by donations row as insiders call for shift in approach
News.content:
Defections, those who leave one party and join another, have been a big part of the party's growth in the last year â not least the recruitment of former Conservative cabinet ministers Robert Jenrick and Suella Braverman.

Elections have been as well - Reform's gains in the English local elections and the devolved parliament elections in Wales and in Scotland.

But so too has money. The backdrop to this conference was the swirl of questions about money even before Channel 4 News', and Verbatim Investigations', endeavours.

In the hour or two before its broadcast on Thursday night, senior Reform figures, including those directly caught up in it, projected a sense of being relatively relaxed about it. Awkward, embarrassing, but survivable.

Once it was broadcast, things changed. There was fury, I am told, and very quickly there was a sense of its gravity. "A few bottles of red were had, and we knew we had to act," is how one source described it to me. The conversations went on into the early hours.

Firstly, there was anger that it would drown out a conference that has been months in the planning. And yes, it has dominated conversation here in Birmingham.

Secondly, there was widespread concern about the image it projected, the impression it would leave.

Reform wants to project itself as a prospective party of government.

And yet the headlines allow critics to claim they are not just ramshackle and amateurish but can point to what looks like a pattern of activity, consciously pursued, to breach the law.

Absolutely not, Nigel Farage insisted to me, there was no such pattern.

But what of the ethos of the party? Journalist Tim Shipman in The Spectator writes , externalthat "it is the experience of everyone I have ever known near the summit of politics that political operations take their character and operating logic from the person at the apex of the triangle. Leaders set culture."

There is something in this. Take Rishi Sunak's Downing Street operation and Boris Johnson's. They were wildly different culturally, reflecting the very different characters at their helm. Would all the things that happened during Partygate under Johnson have happened under Sunak? Unlikely, I would have thought.

Some within Reform, who are full of admiration for Nigel Farage's chutzpah and gift as a communicator, are desperate to see a behind-the-scenes cultural shift that minimises the chances of further embarrassments. And, alongside that, a step up in the infrastructure and personnel to match.

Farage's team express frustration that this is precisely what they have been doing, but some are telling them internally they need to move more quickly.

Both James Orr, the party's head of policy; and Dan Jukes, Farage's right-hand man, will be missed profoundly by those inside the party.

Privately, some wonder if Orr may yet return.

Jukes, who has been a pivotal and loyal figure in Team Farage for years, was already dividing his time between the UK and the United States as his wife and baby are on the other side of the Atlantic.

Perhaps, some senior figures suggest, his immediate future might be in America. Does he return when the general election is nearer? Let's see.

Reform leave Birmingham winded and wounded by the last few days, their days in the sun overshadowed.

The question is how they deal with this and respond to it, in the coming weeks and months.

News.title: Jaguar Land Rover confirms planned job cuts
News.content:
Car manufacturer Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) has confirmed it is opening a voluntary redundancy programme, a year on from a cyber attack which brought production to a halt for more than a month.

The firm said it needed to save about Â£1.7bn over the next two years as it seeks to adapt to "evolving global market conditions".

It was reported by The Times on Saturday that as many as 4,000 jobs may be lost due to the impact of tariffs and a drop in sales.

The firm told the BBC it had not confirmed the numbers. It said the decision to cut jobs was to help "simplify" the organisation as well as "improve efficiency and build greater resilience".

"Today, we informed our colleagues, and trade union partners that JLR is opening a voluntary redundancy programme offering salaried and management team members the opportunity to leave the business," a spokesperson said.

"We will share further information with our colleagues first."

Unite general secretary. Sharon Graham. said the union had been warning about a "perfect storm" hanging over the automotive industry for some time.

"Death by a thousand cuts has been going on under the nose of successive governments," she said.

She added there had been "intensive" discussions over the weekend about mitigating jobs losses adding that she and Business Secretary, Jonathan Reynolds, would be meeting JLR's chief executive, PB Balaji, next week.

"This is an incredibly worrying and stressful time for JLR workers," said Unite national officer, Des Quinn. "Unite is working round the clock to deliver the best possible outcome."

News.title: Trump's response is key as Argentina's Falklands demands get louder
News.content:
Domestic politics can rarely be ruled out of the equation when the Falklands issue flares back up. However, Buenos Aires argues that the matter has become urgent: "A clear and urgent danger", as Milei put it.

With two energy companies â the Israeli-owned Navitas Petroleum and Rockhopper Exploration from the UK â due to undertake work on the Sea Lion oilfield off the Falklands coast within two years, the issue has new impetus. Argentina "cannot allow" the companies to "appropriate the oil reserves under our sea", he said. "We will not stand by with our arms folded," he added.

On Saturday morning Milei's office said on X that it was launching sanctions proceedings against 45 people and companies. The announcement did not identify those targeted and it is not yet clear what impact they will have.

In his speech, Javier Milei painted Argentina as a reliable and "trustworthy partner" to Washington and he enjoys Trump's support, both ideologically and personally.

The two men are close allies in a vision of the Western Hemisphere which Trump calls the "Don-roe Doctrine", a play on words on the 19th Century 'Monroe Doctrine' which exerted American domination over the continent. In essence, the two presidents want to see only like-minded leaders in power in the Americas.

Within such a new partnership and a reordering of the spheres of influence, it's more than conceivable that Trump favours the Argentine leader over the British Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, even if the issues at play transcend personality and party politics.

Perhaps the key question for the coming months, then, is whether the strength of the so-called "Don-roe Doctrine" outweighs the lasting history of the "Special Relationship".

News.title: King and Queen join Highland games fans at Braemar Gathering
News.content:
King Charles and Queen Camilla have joined cheering crowds watching Highland games events at the annual Braemar Gathering in Royal Deeside.

The event, which draws spectators from around the world, is held on the first Saturday of September every year and coincides with the monarch's annual summer holiday at nearby Balmoral.

Among the events watched by the spectators were tug-of-war, caber tossing, hammer throwing, Highland dancing and a parade of pipe bands.

This is the third Games that the King has attended since his coronation.

News.title: Counterfeit weight-loss jabs are booming - and doctors are worried
News.content:
Excitement around the creation of a new drug, especially one showing early promise in clinical trials, is often celebrated by those developing it.

But new weight-loss drug retatrutide has become a headache not only for Eli Lilly, the pharmaceutical company behind it, but for regulators in the UK and around the world.

The jab has not yet been approved for human use by any regulatory body.

But illicit, counterfeit dupes of retatrutide are currently flooding the black market.

Experts have told the BBC this is one of the first times they have seen copycat versions of an experimental drug, still in the throes of being tested, become so widely available.

Vials purporting to be "reta" as it's become known, are being sold in the UK in gyms, nail and beauty salons, hairdressers, on social media and even by flower sellers on the street.

"The world has gone mad," pharmacist and director of 24 HR Pharmacy, Sehar Shahid says. "People are effectively injecting an illegal drug and thinking it's safe.

"It's become so normalised people openly talk about their dealers, where's best to get it from and post all over social media."

One quick flick through my socials and I can order a batch of a drug billed as retatrutide in minutes - although I would have no proof what it's actually made of, what its effects would be and where it's come from.

Keen users are posting before and after "reta" pics on their TikTok feeds, describing how it has silenced food noise, helped them shed pounds and lose inches, with some saying it's completely transformed their lives.

The problem? Despite positive results in its most recent clinical trials, real retatrutide is still being tested for its safety and efficacy.

Only 50% of drugs in this Phase III stage of testing in the US are eventually approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), so there is no guarantee retatrutide will ever hit the market. The high rate of failure is primarily down to drugs not working as well in large, diverse human populations as they do in smaller early tests, or because they reveal unexpected safety hazards.

And the current, fake versions available may not resemble what's being developed in the safe confines of the laboratory.

News.title: Why are European countries moving their gold out of North America?
News.content:
When the central bank of the Netherlands confirmed this week that it had moved tonnes of the country's gold out of North America, it said the relocation would make it "better prepared for severe crises".

Some 86 tonnes from the combined total of about 313 tonnes held in the US and Canada were relocated to London "in view of increasing geopolitical unrest", it said, so the shiny stuff could be "readily available for use in a crisis situation".

Questions were bound to follow. Why were the Dutch doing this? Were they anticipating some major economic shock on the horizon?

It seems not, but the move was clearly in response to the unstable and uncertain state the world finds itself in, with trade and military wars prompting countries to take precautions and hold their gold closer to home.

Earlier this year, France announced it had removed its gold reserves from the US to home shores. Meanwhile, Germany's Bundesbank transferred more than 216 tonnes of the metal from storage locations abroad - 111 tonnes from New York and 105 tonnes from Paris - over a few years ending in 2016., external

It is a strategy which has played out before in times of global instability. "Some European central banks moved part of their gold holdings to New York during the Cold War," said research analysts Lina Thomas and Daan Struyven of Goldman Sachs.

Joseph Cavatoni, senior market strategist at the World Gold Council, told the BBC while wars and trade tensions were "playing into some of these decisions", it didn't "top the list" of motivating factors.

Inflation, interest rates and just having gold in a place where it can be traded quickly also played a role.

"I don't get a sense that there's an impending doom," Cavatoni said, "but what I do think is people are being better educated around how to manage their reserve assets, growing their reserve assets, and actually thinking more effectively around how to make the most of those assets."

De Nederlandsche Bank said the gold removed from the US and Canada between March and August this year was now being held in the vaults of the Bank of England.

"We expect that we will never need to use them, but we do need to strengthen our resilience and preparedness," said the governor of the Dutch central bank, Olaf Sleijpen.

London was seen as the best choice due its position in the world as a major trading centre. If you want to be able to buy or sell gold fast in a crisis, London is the place to be, which makes the Bank of England a popular storage spot.

News.title: UK support for Falkland Islands 'unwavering' after Argentina restates claims, No 10 says
News.content:
It is not yet clear how or to what extent the sanctions will be imposed or tightened. In Argentina, a current law already allows for restrictions of activities of oil companies participating in projects considered unauthorised on the islands.

Two oil companies â Britain's Rockhopper Exploration and Israel's Navitas Petroleum â are due to begin extracting oil in the Sea Lion oilfield off the Falklands coast within two years, something Milei said Argentina could not allow.

A joint statement from the two firms on Friday said it had the valid licences granted by the government of the Falkland Islands, "and with the full support of the UK government."

The project is due to deliver its first oil in 2028, Rockhopper and Navitas said the partnerships' timetable would not be affected.

The Sea Lion oilfield, around 130 miles from the islands, contains an estimated 1.7 billion barrels of oil - described by Rockhopper as a field containing "highly marketable crude".

Milei also announced plans for a naval base in Tierra del Fuego in the south of Argentina, saying Trump and the US were "assessing their historical position in regard to the Falklands", which Argentina refers to as Las Malvinas.

"That is not empty words as they understand that Argentina is a reliable partner and a valuable ally for decades to come," he said, describing the UK as a nation "in decline".

On Thursday, President Trump hinted the US would not help the UK in any future Falklands conflict because Britain "had not been there to help me" during his war with Iran.

Trump's latest remarks on the islands come after he previously said the US position on the Falklands is one of many under review.

On Friday, Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said the UK would "resolutely uphold" the self-determination of the islands.

Writing on X on Friday, Miliband said the Islands would remain British as that is the "overwhelming position of the islanders."

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting also said Britain's commitment to the Falkland Islands was "absolute and unshakeable".

"Milei's statement overnight tells us more about domestic politics in Argentina than it does about the Falkland Islands," he wrote in his own post on X.

In an earlier statement, Downing Street said it was "not the first time" the Argentine government had made economic threats against the Falkland Islands.

"We are clear that the Falkland Islanders' right of self-determination extends to the right to exploit their own natural resources," it said.

Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch said "Britain does not surrender to bullies".

"If (Milei) wants a stronger Argentina, he should build its economy, not threaten others."

Although the US is formally neutral, Washington provided support for Britain's campaign to retake the islands after the Argentinian invasion in 1982.

Argentine forces landed on the Falklands to stake a territorial claim in 1982, sparking a 74-day war over the territory as a British military task force ejected them.

The conflict led to the deaths of 255 British military personnel, three islanders and 649 Argentine military personnel.

In a sign of the ongoing tensions between the two countries over the issue, Argentina players celebrated their victory over England in the World Cup by waving a banner in support of their country's territorial claim.

News.title: Lauryn Hill, Wyclef and Giggs among surprise guests at Jay-Z's long-awaited UK show
News.content:
Jay-Z's first headline solo show in the UK in more than a decade saw him celebrate hip-hop culture alongside a host of special guests, including Lauryn Hill, Wyclef Jean and Giggs.

The US rap superstar rolled back the years for more than two hours - playing hits like 99 Problems, Empire State of Mind and Dead Presidents - as he took to the stage at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Friday night for the first of two shows in London this weekend.

The run is part of his Jay-Z 30 tour, which is marking the 30th anniversary of his debut album, Reasonable Doubt, and his culture-shaping career that followed.

Fans of his wife BeyoncÃ© had hoped she would join him on stage, like she did at two of his three New York shows this summer, as she was also celebrating her 45th birthday on Friday.

News.title: Cleveland police chief proud of force but being 'let down' by funding
News.content:
A Volkswagen Passat carrying five young men drove the wrong way down the motorway near Middlesbrough in the early hours of the morning before colliding with a marked police car.

Officers had been pursuing the car for almost seven minutes after it was connected to earlier alleged criminal activity, but the pursuit was abandoned 10 seconds before the crash when the Passat turned on to the dual carriageway, the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said.

Fuller, whose force covers an area of north-east England that includes Middlesbrough and Teesside, recalled being asleep when the duty commander rang her with the news.

"No matter how tragic and devastated you feel, we swing into action and we do what we need to do," she said.

The home secretary announced this week that Cleveland Police would be given an extra Â£2m to deal with the fallout from the crash, with 200 officers drafted in from elsewhere.

Fuller told the BBC on Friday that she was grateful for the support the force had been given, but added: "I need that all the time."

Cleveland's Labour police and crime commissioner has previously said the force needed an extra Â£20m a year to hire more officers and crack down on organised crime.

Cleveland Police is grappling with the highest recorded crime rate of anywhere in England and Wales, Office for National Statistics (ONS) figures for the year to March show.

It also ranks highest for burglary, sexual offences, violence with injury, and criminal damage and arson.

Fuller said Cleveland Police had also experienced the largest decrease in the number of officers since 2010 and was staffed as if it were a rural force.

"It absolutely needs to change," she said.

Fuller expressed hope that reform to policing across the country was on the horizon, and that Cleveland Police would become one of the "big, strategic forces that have the resource, the flex and the capability to surge when they need to surge".

She added: "In the meantime, we need additional funding... to take us to that point."

Recent inspections show Cleveland is one of the most improved forces in England and Wales, with performance levels also judged to be some of the best in the country.

The force has recently arrested 87 people for offences linked to organised crime gangs and over the past two years 16 people have been jailed for such crimes.

Fuller denied that gangs had control over parts of Middlesbrough, describing it as a "complex" area to police, with high rates of school absence, drug addiction and mental health issues.

"We're doing the very, very best with what we've got - and we absolutely do need more."

Authorities say high deprivation and unemployment in the area are fuelling organised crime.

"When young people have little aspiration or hope, who don't have confidence in the state, then unfortunately criminals exploit these people," Fuller said.

"They give confidence, and they give them hope, and they give them aspiration. And sadly what that means is young people doing things without thought of consequences."

News.title: 'I'd rather die than ring the police': Distrust and fear in Middlesbrough after A66 crash
News.content:
All but one of the residents who speak to us do so on the condition of anonymity. They are worried that showing their faces could place them or their homes at risk.

What message do the attacks send to people on this street, I ask one.

"Well, they should be scared, shouldn't they, that something's going to happen to their property if they say anything or get involved. So we don't."

Victoria, who moved here several years ago, says the escalating violence cannot be separated from the wider condition of the town.

"This is a social problem, especially in this area. Teesside has been massively neglected and ignored," she says.

The attack in Acklam is far from Middlesbrough's only recent case of a vehicle being used as a weapon. Back in May, a tractor was driven into a house on Priory Road, and since the A66 crash Cleveland Police has investigated at least two further rammings.

Detectives have also linked their wider investigation to a caravan fire on Attlee Road in Grangetown.

"It's getting worse," a nearby resident says. "They're always balaclava-ed up as well, do you know what I mean?"

He blames drugs.

"It can't be anything else. Why would you be like you are unless it was drugs?" he says.

Whether every incident is part of a single feud has not been established. But taken together, the rammings, fires and arrests have created a powerful sense that violence is being used to intimidate, punish and send messages.

What is most unsettling for these residents is the sense that nobody is fully in control.

Grangetown and South Bank are communities still living with the void left by the decline of heavy industry. Both now rank among England's most deprived neighbourhoods.

In South Bank, we see a group of teenagers tend three ponies tethered on the grass. Two perform wheelies on electric scooters while another uses a long stick to scatter rubbish.

On the adjoining estate, more than a dozen homes have boarded-up windows.

On a wall are the words "RIP 2UZZI", said locally to have been the nickname of Jakub Matusiak, who lived one street away.

One 17-year-old boy tells us he knew him. "He was my best mate," he says. "It's sad."

Elsewhere, three letters are repeated: "FTP" - an expletive directed at the police.

I ask the teenager if he would call the police if another young person approached him carrying a knife.

"No," he says. Before adding: "I've never needed the police in my life. I'd rather die than ring the police."

Again and again, the young people we speak to express a profound distrust of the police.

Cleveland's Chief Constable Victoria Fuller said what we'd heard was "horrifying".

"Yes, there are a small minority of people in the Grangetown area who blight those communities. But we will continue relentlessly to serve our communities."

The scale of the challenge facing the force and the community it serves is not new.

The area has some of the highest police-recorded crime rates in England and Wales.

Its leaders have been warning for years that its resources did not match the demands placed upon it.

But recent inspections show Cleveland is one of the most improved forces in England and Wales, with performance levels also judged to be some of the best in the country.

The force has recently arrested 87 people for offences linked to organised crime gangs and over the past two years 16 people have been jailed for such crimes.

Since the crash, more than 200 additional officers have been deployed in Middlesbrough and surrounding communities. Their immediate task is to suppress the violence and identify those directing it.

There is also the question of restoring order and rebuilding trust and confidence.

News.title: Reform promises to increase tax-free personal allowance to £15,000
News.content:
Reform UK is promising to increase the tax-free personal allowance to Â£15,000, if it wins the next general election.

Robert Jenrick, the party's economic spokesman, has pledged to introduce the tax cut within the first 100 days if he became chancellor saying it would provide "money that people really need right now".

It is seen by Reform insiders as the flagship policy announcement of its conference and perhaps their biggest tax policy between now and the general election.

Asked about two senior Reform aides being investigated by the party following a Channel 4 News undercover broadcast into claims about funding, Jenrick told the BBC Nigel Farage had acted swiftly and they had been suspended.

In undercover filming by Verbatim Investigations Farage's senior aide Dan Jukes and Reform's head of policy James Orr suggested a way around electoral law to secure foreign party donations for the party, one of which would have totalled Â£500,000.

Electoral law sets out that to be a donor to a UK political party you must be a UK registered voter, or a company registered in the UK.

Farage said on Friday that his party had "done nothing wrong" and had taken "no illegal money. In fact no money was taken at all."

Jukes denied wrongdoing and said he was stepping away from politics "in order to clear my name". Orr told Sky News he would cooperate fully with the party's internal investigation.

Orr is an associate professor of Philosophy of Religion at Cambridge University's Faculty of Divinity, and responding to the Channel 4 News and Verbatim report, Cambridge University said it was "looking into these matters".

Jenrick told the Today programme that the party had taken legal advice and it did not believe it had done anything wrong.

Labour and the Liberal Democrats have reported the party to the Metropolitan Police.

The Electoral Commission has said it is considering "all relevant information, in line with our regulatory remit" and was in contact with the police.

News.title: Tonnes of rubble including 'bits of old toilets' being dumped in village, residents claim
News.content:
Wrexham Council has also issued a temporary stop notice after a "significant amount" of material was deposited "without planning permission".

The council said it would also be serving enforcement and stop notices "to remedy the situation and have the land restored".

Tom Lawson, from Coedpoeth, said he was frustrated that the activity was not stopped by NRW when it was first spotted.

He estimated there were thousands of tonnes of material, which he said looked like "low-grade demolition waste", saying that he had seen tar and lead batteries in amongst the rubble.

He said he also feared the people responsible would "just walk away from it".

"It'll be left for the public to pay... it's just wrong," he said.

Wrexham-based company SOS Aggregates said it owned the land in Coedpoeth and had been depositing "grade 1A fill material" on the site to make a plateau on which to create the equine arena which would then be "landscaped".

A spokesman for the firm denied it had continued depositing on the site when the temporary stop order was in place, but said it had continued work once the order expired.

He said that they had told the council they would be submitting a planning application this week and that they were also seeking legal advice.

He said the company would also be providing evidence to NRW of the materials being used on the site.

The investigations in Coedpoeth come as another field on the edge of the nearby village of Minera has seen dozens of lorries depositing materials, which one local councillor described as "reeking of diesel".

Caravans have also been placed on the site opposite a cul-de-sac of bungalows on Nantlais.

The farmland was sold approximately two months ago, but according to the council no planning application has been submitted for development there.

SOS Aggregates said it had delivered recycled construction material to the site in Minera, but that it was not involved in work taking place there and did not own the land.

Wrexham Council has served a temporary stop notice due to "a breach of planning control and the change of use of the land to a gypsy and traveller site with associated engineering operations".

NRW said it was investigating the materials on the site and would take action if appropriate.

News.title: Moment mum catches suspected arson attack on CCTV
News.content:
A mum-of-two has said she was "disgusted" after watching CCTV of an arson attacker setting fire to her home.

Holly Cham, 33, from Bootle, in Merseyside, was away with her children when - in an incident caught on her security cameras - a stranger appeared to emerge from her garage, coming back into view as a fire took hold.

A 31-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of arson with intent to endanger life following a fire on 24 August, Merseyside Police said.

He was released on conditional bail pending further enquiries, the force said.

News.title: The Grand Tour's new presenters: 'I hope we prove the critics wrong'
News.content:
For a show built around the chemistry of its three former presenters, finding a replacement trio with such chemistry was always going to be as important as finding people who knew about cars.

Engelsman and Holland are an already established double act as the presenters of Throttle House, a motoring YouTube channel with more than three million subscribers.

The bigger unknown was who would become their third presenter.

That search eventually led the show's producers to Francis Bourgeois, a social media star better known for standing on railway platforms than behind the wheel of a supercar.

Engelsman says he and Holland had done chemistry testing with a number of people, but Bourgeois immediately felt different.

"As soon as Francis showed up, we were like: 'That guy'," Holland says.

Bourgeois remembers their first meeting taking place on a leather sofa in a hotel outside Basingstoke, where they mostly talked about what cars they owned.

By the time filming began, Holland says there was no need to consciously work out how to make the three-person dynamic function as "it just worked and clicked immediately".

While the chemistry came quickly, actually finding out they had the job was much less straightforward. Engelsman says there was "no immediate moment" when they were formally told they had been chosen.

"It was the most gradual thing," he says.

He and Holland initially thought they were simply part of a wider audition process, but then found themselves repeatedly being invited into writers' rooms and asked for their views on ideas for the show.

For Bourgeois, that uncertainty may have been helpful as he admits he'd "just fall apart and start crying" if he'd found out about the job.

There is a clear generational shift with the new presenters, all three of whom built their profiles on social media - and critics have been mixed on how successfully that translates to The Grand Tour.

The Independent's three-star review, external described the reboot as "all rather safe" and said the presenters feel "stilted".

The Guardian's review, external agreed and called the trio a "decent, if slightly anonymous, presence" who seem "quite meek and pleasant, and without any obvious dynamic".

But it did praise Bourgeois, with Stuart Heritage calling him "the most enthusiastic enthusiast currently working on planet Earth".

The FT also awarded the show three-stars, external and said that while the big budget spectacles are enjoyable to watch, they also feel "a little muted".

It added that "the real question is whether a series that has been driven by big personalities like Clarkson, May and Hammond can survive with a new team".

Hammond tells BBC News he tuned in for The Grand Tour's return and said it was great to see the new team getting going.

"That's the most important thing for them is to make their show. We made our show and we're really good at being us. They're going to be really good at being them," he says.

Hammond says the audience need to "give them the chance" to show that.

South Africa and New Zealand collide in the third Test of a heated Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series that continues to deliver thrills and drama.

News.content:

Police have started a murder probe following the death of a man in South London.

The Metropolitan Police said officers were called to an address in Poynders Road, Lambeth, at around 8.35pm on Friday after a report from the London Fire Brigade.

A man in his 30s was found with serious head injuries and was subsequently pronounced dead at the scene.

Detective chief inspector Alison Foxwell said: “At this stage, we believe this was an isolated incident and there is no evidence to suggest any wider risk to the public.

open image in gallery The Met Police have launched a murder investigation ( AFP/Getty )

“I would urge anyone who was in the area, or who may have seen or heard anything unusual, to come forward and speak to us.

“Even the smallest piece of information could prove vital in helping us understand the circumstances surrounding this man’s death.”

A London Fire Brigade spokesperson added: “The brigade was called to effect an entry to a property on Poynders Road, Lambeth.

“Upon gaining entry, firefighters discovered the body of a man in the property. Despite the efforts of firefighters and paramedics, he was declared dead at the scene.”

Pierre Gasly delivered the shock of the season by taking the first pole position of his career for Sunday’s Italian Grand Prix.

Gasly’s improbable triumph arrived a day on from his Alpine boss Flavio Briatore accusing an FIA judge of having a “working relationship” with McLaren after the British team’s appeal saw the Frenchman stripped of his podium from June’s Monaco Grand Prix.

George Russell, widely expected to claim a much-needed pole in his world championship quest, had to settle for second, pipped to top spot by Gasly by just 0.060 seconds.

McLaren’s Oscar Piastri finished third, with Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton fourth and fifth respectively for Ferrari.

Championship leader Kimi Antonelli took seventh but will start his home race from the back of the grid as he serves an engine penalty.

World champion Lando Norris arrived in Italy with consecutive victories under his belt but looks almost certain to miss out on a hat-trick after he could manage only ninth.

With Antonelli starting Sunday’s 53-lap race from the rear, Russell knew this event would hand him a golden chance to eat into his Mercedes team-mate’s 59-point championship lead.

But the Englishman will have to see off Gasly’s unexpected challenge to claim a full quota of points in what could prove a pivotal contest in the title race with 11 rounds, including Sunday’s fixture, still to go.

Hamilton spoke about his dream of winning in Monza for a record sixth time and a first for Ferrari in the build-up to the Italian team’s home event.

open image in gallery Gasly celebrates his shock pole ( AP )

But the seven-time world champion endured a difficult afternoon for Ferrari in their own backyard.

Top-10 - Italian GP qualifying 1. Pierre Gasly (Alpine) 2. George Russell (Mercedes) 3. Oscar Piastri (McLaren) 4. Charles Leclerc (Ferrari) 5. Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari) 6. Max Verstappen (Red Bull) 7. Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes)* 8. Franco Colapinto (Alpine) 9. Lando Norris (McLaren) 10. Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls) *Will start at the back of the grid due to an engine penalty

At one stage, Hamilton’s presence in Q3 appeared in grave danger after he could set only the 10th quickest time, with Audi’s Gabriel Bortoleto set to hand him a humiliating exit.

However, his blushes were spared by just one thousandth of a second.

“We are through,” said Hamilton’s race engineer, Carlo Santi. “That was very tight.”

“Ah, f*** me,” said Hamilton in response. His first run in Q3 left him in ninth, almost eight tenths off the pace, but he improved with his second to haul him up the order, 0.225 sec slower than Gasly.

It was an unsatisfactory afternoon for Red Bull with Max Verstappen – who claimed his car was “broken” and “undriveable” – three tenths off the pace in sixth.

While Liam Lawson, who continues to deputise for Isack Hadjar – currently sidelined with a wrist injury – accused Red Bull of leaving him “out to dry” after he was knocked out in Q2.

open image in gallery Lewis Hamilton could only qualify fifth

But there were no such concerns for Gasly as he flourished in his Alpine.

“I have been waiting for that one,” yelled the Frenchman – whose sole victory of his Formula One life arrived in Monza six years ago – over the radio.

And he will start from the perfect position to claim a second career win, albeit this time for Alpine, rather than AlphaTauri, when the lights go out on Sunday.

Fernando Alonso finished ninth at the previous round to raise hopes of an Aston Martin revival. But the double world champion qualified 21st, with only team-mate Lance Stroll slower.

Williams’ poor run also continued with Alex Albon eliminated in Q1 in 18th and Carlos Sainz just scraping through to the second phase. Sainz was 15th in the end, while Albon will move to the back as he joins Antonelli and Lawson in serving an engine penalty.

The owner of Tetris criticized the Trump administration after the White House released an arcade game titled “Build the Wall” on its official website.

The game, which appeared on the White House website this week, mimics the mechanics of the classic Tetris, letting players rotate and stack falling blocks. But in this version, users are tasked with constructing a wall along the U.S.-Mexico border to repel a “Zombie Border Siege.” If users fail, a message appears reading: “Border Breached.”

“At Tetris we believe in the power of connection and bringing people together, not dividing them. To our fans everywhere: we love you, we see you, and we’re grateful to have you in our community,” the Tetris brand said in a statement posted to social media on Friday.

The company stressed it had no role in creating the White House game and warned that it takes “copyright infringement very seriously.”

When asked by Variety whether the company had considered taking legal action, a spokesperson said Tetris was “currently reviewing the matter.”

open image in gallery The owner of Tetris lashed out at the Trump administration after a 'Build The Wall' arcade game appeared on the White House's website ( Whitehouse.gov )

The Independent has contacted the White House for comment.

The game rolled out Thursday as part of a batch of White House arcade titles, including one dubbed “Supply Run” that lets players assemble school meals tied to the “Make America Healthy Again” initiative. Another called “Rio Run” puts users in the role of Border Patrol agents along the Rio Grande.

In a post on X unveiling the games, the White House wrote: “Can’t stop winning.”

open image in gallery In the ‘Build The Wall’ game, users are tasked with constructing a Tetris-style structure to repel a ‘Zombie Border Siege’ ( Whitehouse.gov )

The White House’s communications strategy has long leaned on employing pop culture imagery — particularly in its attempt to promote the president’s immigration crackdown, which polls indicate is unpopular with many Americans.

Earlier this year, it posted a video likening ICE agents to Spider-Man, with detainees shown ensnared in webs. And last year, capitalizing on a social-media trend, the White House shared a Studio Ghibli-style illustration of a detained migrant.

In the past, the use of such imagery has resulted in pushback from companies.

For instance, in 2018, the president posted “Sanctions are coming” on Twitter, seemingly referencing Game of Thrones’ “Winter is coming” tagline. The font appeared similar to that used by the hit HBO show.

“We were not aware of this messaging and would prefer our trademark not be misappropriated for political purposes,” HBO said in response, according to Time.

The Oasis reunion is thriving more than ever, with the Gallagher brothers looking like the best of friends ahead of the premiere of their new documentary.

In a sight that would have been unthinkable two years ago, Noel Gallagher and Liam Gallagher arrived at a Venice Film Festival photocall on Saturday (5 September) together, posing with their arms around each other.

Noel went so far as to describe Liam as “delightful” – a word he conceded he “never would have thought” he’d say about him.

open image in gallery Noel and Liam Gallagher are friendlier than ever ( Getty Images )

Sharing an insight into their reconciliation, he told Daily Mail: “All the little things that used to annoy us about each other have gone away. We have come out of it now as equals.”

He added: “We get along now, we text like normal people. The music brought us together.”

The new documentary, titled Oasis: Don't Look Back in Anger, will explore the story of their reunion, which turned into a high-profile 2025 tour. The premiere follows reports that the musician siblings will soon announce more shows for next year, which the pair appear to have been teasing this week.

For the project, Peaky Blinders creator Steven Knight was granted behind-the-scenes access as once-warring brothers Noel and Liam Gallagher rehearsed and were reunited onstage for the first time since the band’s split in 2009.

In a new interview, Knight, who is also writing the next James Bond film, said he believed that the brothers’ getting older had helped them bury their animosity towards one another.

open image in gallery Oasis stars are set to premiere new music documentary at Venice Film Festival ( Getty Images )

“You start throwing all this crap away,” he told the Times. “In your twenties you’re so full of it, angry and easily offended. Then you get older and realise: all that’s left is who you really are.

“And it became apparent, during the tour, that Noel and Liam are similar people. They’re both very funny and they speak the truth.”

In the same interview, Knight said that Noel had “no idea” there would be such interest in an Oasis reunion: “They hadn’t recorded anything for years, they hadn’t been promoting the old albums, but the music had been passed down through generations in their absence.”

Noel apparently cast doubt on the idea of the band playing stadiums. “He thought they’d be playing arenas,” Knight said. “The second shock came when Liam and Noel first went out on stage at Cardiff and felt the emotion. People were in tears.”

Don’t Look Back in Anger is in cinemas from 9 September.

News.content:
