World.title: FACT CHECK: Sara Duterte not in handcuffs for grave threats arrest; circulating photo is altered
World.content:
The altered photo was from her visit to Ateneo de Zamboanga University following the August 18 shooting incident

Claim: Vice President Sara Duterte was seen wearing handcuffs before posting bail as the Quezon City Regional Trial Court ordered her arrest on three counts of grave threat on September 4.

Rating: ALTERED

Why we fact-checked this: Multiple posts have used the photo and appeared to show that Duterte has finally been arrested and put in handcuffs before posting bail.

Facebook user Atty Joel Rodriguez Dizon, a Baguio-based lawyer, posted the photo with a caption that read, “She made bail. But I have to admit it does give you some measure of quiet satisfaction even for just a tiny moment to see this woman in handcuffs.”

The post has 4,400 reactions and 928 shares as of writing.

Facebook page Trendline PH also wrote in its post, “Be honest, how do you feel seeing her in handcuffs even just for a short while (because she was able to post bail)?”

User Tomboc Urbiztondo Ed posted it in a Facebook group, copied Dizon’s caption, then added: “Guys, nagbayad na ng bail si VP Sara Duterte. Bakit may posas pa siya? Sa mga 32 million na bumoto, guys, anong masasabi ninyo dito?”

(Guys, VP Sara Duterte has already posted bail. Why is she still in handcuffs? To the 32 million who voted for her—guys, what do you have to say about this?)

The other two posts garnered 1,046 reactions, 513 comments, and 78 shares.

The image, accompanied by similar captions, was likewise circulated by various other Facebook accounts and pages.

The facts: The original photo was from Duterte’s visit to Ateneo de Zamboanga University following the August 18 shooting incident. Duterte was not seen wearing handcuffs when she arrived at the Quezon City RTC Branch 98 to post bail.

Duterte shared photos of her school visit in a Facebook post, including the original version of the altered photo where she talked to university president Fr. Guillrey Andal and police officers.

Upon posting bail, Duterte told reporters she does “not feel safe” with the police personnel deployed in the court.

The court ordered Duterte’s arrest for three counts of grave threats in August following complaints from the National Bureau of Investigation over Duterte’s November 23, 2024, midnight press conference.

During that press conference, Duterte said she had already talked to someone who would kill President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., his wife, and Romualdez if she herself were killed.

Altered through AI: The photo was altered with the use of artificial intelligence (AI). AI detection tool SightEngine flagged it as 99% AI-generated, while HiveDetect said it is 59.7% likely to be AI.

Duterte’s impeachment trial: Duterte’s grave threats case is cited as the fourth article of impeachment, or cases against her, at the Senate impeachment court.

According to experts, Duterte’s case under the Quezon City RTC will not affect the ongoing impeachment trial because the impeachment process is different from criminal proceedings.

– Eirene Manatlao/Rappler.com

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

World.title: Your cat or dog can now fly with you on Philippine Airlines domestic flights
World.content:
Fur parents, rejoice! Both small cats and dogs are now cleared for takeoff on all local PAL flights

MANILA, Philippines – Philippine Airlines (PAL) passengers can now bring their cat or dog along for domestic trips, with the flag carrier expanding its FurPAL in-cabin pet program to include both small cats and dogs.

For P2,500 one way, passengers may bring one small dog or cat inside the cabin on PAL domestic flights, subject to aircraft availability and the airline’s pet limits.

There are a few things to remember before you book your cat’s next flight.

Pets must be at least 12 weeks old and fully weaned, while the combined weight of the animal and its carrier cannot exceed 10 kilograms. They must be inside a soft-sided carrier, measuring no more than 45 x 25 x 28 centimeters, that can fit beneath the seat and be roomy enough for the pet to stand, turn around, and lie down comfortably.

Pet parents also have some paperwork to prepare. At check-in, PAL requires:

A signed declaration and waiver

A veterinary health certificate issued within five days of departure

A valid anti-rabies vaccination certificate

A Bureau of Animal Industry local shipping permit

Once aboard, cats and dogs must stay inside their carriers under the seat for the entire flight. So, sorry, hooman, no lap time or mid-flight photoshoots allowed. Buying your pet its own seat is also not an option.

Pets may drink water but can’t be fed airline food, so owners are advised to feed them before departure. Dogs must also have diapers on, while cats must have absorbent pads in their carriers.

FurPAL is limited to approved aircraft, including PAL’s Q400, A320, A321ceo, certain A330s, Boeing 777s and A350s. Space is also scarce. Most approved aircraft can carry only up to three pets per flight, so you need to be book and pay at least 48 hours before departure.

Travelers can check PAL’s full FurPAL terms and FAQs for the complete rules before booking. – Rappler.com

World.title: How ‘Filipiñana’s’ slow burn exposes the Philippines’ class divide
World.content:
Content warning: Minor spoilers ahead.

Filipinos have a complex relationship with the tropical heat.

We’re used to getting sweaty all our lives, even during the times we don’t even move that much: sitting in random establishments, wandering idly in our homes, or standing in line, waiting for something (an activity Filipinos have been well accustomed to, because everything feels ironically slow in our fast-paced society).

But as mundane as it may seem, the extreme temperature isn’t to be underestimated. A Greenpeace report shows that heat stress is pushing Filipinos into a “climate poverty trap.” Heat has lingered in our lives so much that it has caused class suspensions and economical disruptions, among other things.

In the Filipino film Filipiñana, though, heat isn’t only a villain; it’s a catalyst to expose bigger evils. The satirical debut feature of Rafael Manuel — who also wrote and edited the film — follows Isabel (played by Jorrybell Agoto), a 17-year-old “tee girl” who’s new to the job in an exclusive country club. Her responsibilities include assisting golfers in setting up golf balls at the hitting bay. One of them is Dr. Palanca (Teroy Guzman), the club’s president, whom Isabel gets strangely drawn to.

Jorrybell Agoto stars as a 17-year-old tee girl. Filipiñana film still

Before hitting the local cinemas, Filipiñana graced the international festival circuit through the Sundance Film Festival — where it took home the Special Jury Award for Creative Vision — and the 76th Berlinale.

Bianca Balbuena, one of the film’s producers and CEO of Epicmedia Productions Inc., shared in an interview with Rappler: “This is the project where I got to deal with big studios mostly doing English-speaking films, the complicated but rewarding UK system of legal, financing, and closing.”

“We also have a UK distributor, BFI [Distribution], so I am excited to discover a wider UK audience. I am also learning a lot from our Oscar-winning distributor Kino Lorber and our PR companies in North America, Divergent and Cinetic, on how to push and market our local films to the Western market.”

The paradox of water

Filipiñana happens over the course of one day. It starts off strong with its juxtaposition of two contrasting scenes, showing class disparity. There’s a cramped Manila neighborhood where residents scurry to fill their jugs with water, a scarce resource. Their chaotic state gets even more rattling when they almost get hit by a tourist van, ridden by the country club visitors, who are protected from the drought thanks to their air conditioning.

Meanwhile, the golf course catering to high society has an abundance of water — sprinklers and water fountains are for everyone’s convenience, even to the rich who can’t seem to stop complaining: “Grabe, ang init, parang galit na galit ang Diyos sa atin (Wow, it’s so hot, it’s like God is so angry at us).”

Thirst is a strong emotion in the film, and is experienced by almost everyone — whether it’s for a new discovery, self-expression, or personal fulfillment. Everyone can’t seem to feel satisfied with what they have now, and are always left wanting more.

But you’ll have more empathy for the tee girls who’d put themselves in discomfort, just to catch some cold air conditioning because their electric fans won’t cut it in the sweltering heat.

For a relatively quiet film, it told a lot.

A reasonable slow burn

Filipiñana had its Cinemalaya 2026 run as the festival’s closing film, its Philippine premiere, with some critics pointing out how it’s awfully slow, that you could easily fall asleep before the credits roll.

While its slow pace is heavily felt, it’s intelligently done, as it lies in intention. Its slowness probably means lethargy — how the extreme heat pushes you to take things in slowly, or discourages you to take action.

“As our great cinema icon Lav Diaz says: ‘It’s just cinema.’ We feel that to group a film into a category just based on the pace of the film would do a great disservice to the audience,” Balbuena said.

“There are so many kinds of films to explore and discover. We would say don’t be fooled by the term ‘slow cinema’. It can move you with incredible emotion and even overwhelming violence. Pacing and technique are just ways to tell a story,” she added.

“Filipiñana is different from most films we’re used to as [a] general audience, because the film is more formalist than narrative. It takes a certain kind of openness to accept that. And that is, in fact, counterflow cinema.”

Since the POV we’re following is Isabel’s, the slow burn also makes sense. It’s her first day on the job, and for someone so young in that disposition, it would take some time to absorb (and revisit) some horrors.

“For us, it’s always been about the portrayal of innocence — about innocence lost but ultimately, humanity gained,” Balbuena stated.

“The film is a coming-of-age. Her growing up has a lot to do with her turning inward into memories, which she has suppressed or forgotten. This is a representative of a malaise plaguing our country — we have a short collective memory as people.”

Picturesque eeriness

Even if the film’s audience is torn between liking or disliking its pace, what they can probably agree on is that it’s the epitome of picturesque. Every frame packs striking color palettes, flawless blocking, and overall jaw dropping production design. This reflects the team’s ambitious creative choices.

“I’ve also learned that when we have big support, we can do production the proper way. We shot for over 50 days in eight golf courses and took care of the well-being of the staff and cast. We do rehearsals in the morning and shoot in the afternoon. It was a breath of fresh air — how this production was run,” said Balbuena.

Does this make perfectionism a healthy trait to cultivate in filmmaking?

“[It] depends on the goal and purpose. If it’s perfectionism with the goal of doing things the right way based on a moral stance, then yes. But we also believe perfectionism is the enemy of creativity,” argued Balbuena.

Perfectionism also spilled over to the movie. There’s an eerie kind of synchronization in the actions made by the swimming pool cleaners to the staffers fixing the chairs and tables. Everything is well-choreographed, as if to cover something dark and twisted.

Ilocos as an anchor

As both Isabel and Dr. Palanca hail from Ilocos, you’d initially think that this becomes a sacred similarity. However, this profound (one-sided) connection also becomes Isabel’s portal to a wakeup call, as exhibited to the timing of when “Manang Biday,” a traditional Ilocano folk song, plays in the film.

“Ilocos, as you already know, is a rural northern region in the Philippines that is of immense political significance — it’s where infamous dictator Ferdinand Marcos hails from,” explained Balbuena. “And now, less than 40 years after he was ousted from power, his son is the current president of the Philippines. Ilocos is also where Jorrybell Agoto, who plays Isabel, was born. So it was a very natural choice.”

A post-colonialism portrait

Ultimately, Filipiñana portrays Philippine society rooted in American colonialism. And it’s a clever creative choice to inject it right in the title.

“When you look up ‘Filipiñana’ in a dictionary, it’s defined as anything that relates to Filipino culture and I liked the juxtaposition of matching that with the image of a golf course,” Manuel tells Rappler. “Because although it’s not the first thing that comes to mind when one thinks of the Philippines, I think a golf course encapsulates our country quite well. I also think of it as a play on Americana but with an “ñ” (which is used in Spanish) so with one word — “Filipiñana” — you allude to both our colonial histories.”

But zooming into the film, you’ll feel that this isn’t where it all ends. When a default Mandarin greeting gets repeatedly taught to the tee girls to welcome Chinese tourists — to the point that it almost feels robotic — you could sense how Isabel suddenly wants to take control of what she can, even in ways you can’t explain.

So, you almost completely get it when she hits a mango with a golf club, or jumps into unknown waters, just to feel something. – Rappler.com

World.title: Gamified abuse: How a PH forum rewards submissions of non-consensual intimate content
World.content:
By its structure, the system has the effect of encouraging members to find material worth posting, whether by obtaining videos from former partners, redistributing Telegram content, or manipulating women into sending intimate images. The more active a member becomes, the more they stand to gain within the community.

On NSFWPH, however, those incentives revolve around something more concerning: the non-consensual sharing of intimate content.

Higher-ranked members may gain access to locked content, including additional information attached to posts such as the names of victims or links to their Facebook and Instagram accounts.

Users who accumulate enough points are promoted through ranks such as "Established Member," "Elite," "Contributor," and eventually "Legendary," the forum's highest status.

Members create threads. They comment. They react to posts. They earn points. And every interaction contributes toward a merit system that unlocks additional privileges.

The forum, which now boasts more than 430,000 registered members, has evolved into far more than a repository of intimate images and videos. It is a structured online community where users are rewarded for posting content, climbing membership ranks through participation, and, in some cases, monetizing the very intimate images they upload.

It's because there is something to gain. For the operators of NSFWPH, it is traffic.

"Why would someone share something that was never theirs in the first place?"

"I am hurt by the fact that they took something so private, deeply private, to gain attention or to make money," she said.

Shortly after discovering that intimate videos of her had been uploaded online, Mishy kept returning to a question.

The following story contains descriptions and discussions of sexual violence, image-based abuse, and the non-consensual sharing and explicit sexualization of women. Reader discretion is advised.

Access costs P500, according to a post by Mikeykun on his Discord channel called Mikey's Vault, payable through GCash. In return, members receive download links to additional content.

His two Discord servers â Mikey's Vault and The Nowhere â collectively host nearly 6,000 members. One advertises a VIP-only section offering "Exclusive" and "SHS" (senior high school) sets to paying members. His Facebook page has 4,400 followers.

Under the same identity, he maintains Facebook pages and Discord communities where followers are directed toward additional content. In one Facebook post, he reminded users he had referred to NSFWPH to follow the forum's rules because violations could affect his own account. In another, he told followers he would focus less on updating NSFWPH and instead devote more attention to his Discord server, The Nowhere.

What this illustrates is that content is not simply exchanged; it also generates income for some, in this case, Mikey Kun.

Theoretically, if 100 of those 200 posts reach at least 1,000 clicks on shrinkme.io links, that would mean Kun earned $400 or roughly P24,000 (at $1 = P60).

In our scan, Kun had more than 200 posts with corresponding shrinkme.io links just in July and August 2026. In our random sampling of these posts, the majority reach at least 1,000 views on the forum, with one post reaching at least 12,000, while a few reach only 600 or 700 views.

Shrinkme.io's official payout rates vary by country. In the Philippines, the rate is US$4 per 1,000 views.

To download one of Kun's videos, a user clicks on a shrinkme.io link associated with a specific post. The user is then redirected to a series of pop-up ads before they eventually reach the actual download link. For every 1,000 users that click the link, Kun is given a payout.

Kun holds the rank of "Legendary," the highest attainable status in the forum. He has amassed 4,902 posts â the third-highest post count on the site. Included among those uploads are sexually explicit videos of Filipina women, ranging from livestreamers on livestreaming platform BIGO to content described as "leaks" and "scandals."

Rappler identified one of the platform's most prolific contributors: a user known as Mikey Kun.

According to analytics service Semrush, NSFWPH receives more than 10 million page views each month, with users viewing an average of 25 pages per visit and remaining on the site for over 14 minutes.

Users gain prestige in the forum. They earn advertising revenue through download links and also by selling access to the seller's collections directly on other channels.

The website displays multiple s on every page using ExoClick, an advertising network commonly used by adult websites. ExoClick estimates earnings of roughly $500 for every 3-5 million ad views, although actual revenues vary, depending on factors such as location and conversion rates. Each page on NSFWPH displays around five s.

The figures do not reveal exactly how much the site earns but they do show that this amount of traffic has commercial value.

Together, they sustain a platform whose popularity depends on the continued circulation of intimate content â the origin of which are often questionable.

What the law says

Despite the apparent business built around these images and videos, Philippine law already prohibits much of the conduct taking place.

The Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism Act of 2009 makes it illegal not only to record sexual acts or private parts without consent, but also to copy, distribute, publish, sell, or broadcast such recordings without the written consent of everyone involved â even if the recording itself was initially consensual.

The later Safe Spaces Act further strengthened protections by penalizing gender-based online harassment, including the non-consensual uploading or sharing of photos, audio, or videos with sexual content.

Lawyer Dana Batnag, data privacy expert and human rights advocate, discussed further the elements of proper consent. "First, consent has to be informed. You need to tell me your purpose [for recording or documenting]. Consent has to be specific. A person can consent to documentation, but not for posting. If you were manipulated [to share intimate content], then was that consent freely given? Consent must also be freely given."

Consent to take a photo or record a video doesn't mean that the person has also given consent to have the content distributed, shared, or posted by any means. Persons also have the right to retract that right at any time they want.

Respicio Law also states: "A person who receives leaked private photos and forwards them may also face liability. 'I only shared it' is not always a defenseâ¦ Group chat members, page admins, channel operators, and social media users should not repost, save, mock, or circulate intimate images."

Based on data privacy laws, Batnag said that since the forum is trafficking sensitive personal information in the form of intimate photos and videos, the administrators and owners of the site should be identified.

"For example, I'm one of those women. I have the right to know, under the data subjects right, who looked at my picture, who gave it to you, how you got it, your source of information. And I have the right to know to whom you shared those. As the data subject, I can demand that right. I can demand it from the owner of the website," the lawyer explained.

The site allows users to request for a content takedown, but since these are intimate images that are considered sensitive personal information, that would also mean that when the thousands of users get to see them without the clear and express permission of the subject, it can be argued that a violative breach of privacy has occurred.

Batnag also said that even if the website was hosted in another country, the owners of the website would face consequences under the Data Privacy Act, as the site deals with information of Filipinos, not just of the potential women victims, but also the very users registered on the site.

According to Liza Garcia, executive director of the Foundation for Media Alternatives, who advocates against the non-consensual sharing of intimate images, a massive platform like NSFWPH inflicts "a lot of harm" on victims, particularly young women, who often suffer profound "emotional harm" and "psychological harm."

Beyond the immediate trauma, victims face severe "harm to reputation" and even "financial harm" because the public nature of the exploitation can result in a victim being unable to work: "hindi ka na makapagtrabaho, ayaw mo na kasing lumabas ng bahay, nahiya ka na" (you can no longer work, you no longer want to leave the house, you are already ashamed).

This "profound shame" often causes victims to "tend to isolate" themselves, which means the "economic aspect of [their] life" is deeply affected.

This is the potential damage that can be caused by the operation of such a website.

For Garcia, those harms are not hypothetical. They are the foreseeable consequence of a platform built around the circulation of intimate content.

For the Philippine National Police Anti-Cybercrime Group (PNP-ACG), NSFWPH is part of a broader landscape of online sexual exploitation and non-consensual sharing of intimate material.

The police have been actively pursuing perpetrators. From 2025 through August 2026, the PNP-ACG conducted 138 operations involving cyber warrants, entrapment operations, arrest warrants, and rescue operations, resulting in the arrest of 160 individuals involved in violations of the Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism Act.

Authorities also rescued minors and apprehended seven children in conflict with the law (CICL) related to these cases.

But going after NSFWPH itself presents a different challenge: jurisdiction.

A quick check on forensic tool Domaintools.com showed that the IP address of NSFWPH is connected to a Cloudflare server in San Francisco, California. Asueta said since the forum is hosted outside the Philippines, it is difficult for Philippine authorities to directly compel the platform to act. "So this is a jurisdictional issue," he said.

Requests for takedowns can also be circumvented through new sites and VPNs.

Asueta said these activities have existed for "medyo matagal-tagal na rin" (for quite a long time already). Recently, the PNP-ACG has seen fewer reports about the non-consensual spread of intimate images within its unit but cautioned that this does not necessarily mean the problem is declining because some victims may simply not be reporting.

Server accountability

Victims still have some recourse with content found on NSFWPH. The PNP-ACG said victims can file a complaint, and investigators can attempt to trace the source of the material found on the forum, identify an individual suspect, and pursue a case.

The police can also apply for a cyber warrant to search and examine the suspect's cellphone or computer for evidence.

But again, going after the actual platform is harder. Right now, if investigators can gather sufficient evidence, Asueta said they can coordinate with the relevant jurisdiction through Interpol and the International Mutual Legal Assistance mechanism â a formal method for international cooperation under the Department of Justice.

However, in the longer term, Asueta called for laws requiring foreign platforms operating in the Philippines to establish local offices and submit to Philippine court processes such as warrants and subpoenas.

To other women who may one day find themselves in the same position, Mishy offered fighting words: "Your body is not your shame. You deserve to take up space in this world without apologizing for what someone else did to you. There are countless women standing beside you, silently carrying the same wounds â but all of us are still worthy of every beautiful thing life has to offer. What happened to you is not a reflection of your worth."

Mishy said that if she had enough proof or evidence on who leaked the videos, she would attempt to pursue a legal case. â Rappler.com

Lance Ariel Bustos is an Aries Rufo Journalism Fellow for 2026, currently studying at the De La Salle University Manila.

World.title: Sara Duterte posts bail for grave threats case
World.content:
POSTING BAIL. Vice President Sara Duterte, along with legal counsels, arrives at the Quezon City Regional Trial Court, following the issuance of an arrest warrant against her over a grave threats case, on September 5, 2026.

(1st UPDATE) The Vice President posts bail a day after a Quezon City court issued warrants for her arrest over three counts of grave threats

MANILA, Philippines – Vice President Sara Duterte posted bail on Saturday, September 5, in connection with the three counts of grave threats filed against her over her alleged assassination threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., First Lady Liza Marcos, and former House speaker Martin Romualdez.

Her lawyer, Paul Lawrence Lim, confirmed that Duterte posted P120,000 bail for each count of grave threat before Quezon City Regional Trial Court Branch 98.

Lim said Duterte underwent booking process inside the court, which includes taking of her fingerprints.

“Kailangan pa rin (It’s necessary)…. [She did the booking process] in front of court staff,” Lim told reporters outside the court.

Duterte’s impeachment lawyer and spokesperson Michael Poa was also present in court with Duterte and Lim. The two lawyers, in a statement, said, “After receiving all bail requirements, the court issued an order lifting the arrest warrant.”

Play Video

Before entering the hall, Duterte talked to journalists where she aired concerns over her security.

“I have documented threats and harassment since 2023. I fear for my children. I do not feel they are safe if I am with them. Umalis na nga ako kung nasaan mga anak ko para pumunta sa korte pero pumunta pa rin ang pulis. I do not feel safe. Pakiramdam ko papatayin nila ako,” Duterte said in a statement.

(I left the place where my children are to go to the court but the police still came… I feel like they will kill me.)

After she posted bail, Duterte said in a media interview that her lawyers had presented all possible scenarios in connected to the arrest warrant and advised her, “Magbail ka para maprotektahan ka ng taongbayan (Post bail so that the people can protect you).”

She also motioned to the police personnel deployed to the court that day and reiterated that she does “not feel safe with all these police personnel.”

Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) Secretary Jonvic Remulla later responded to the Vice President’s statements: “It’s very unfortunate that all the pressure in her life is affecting her perception. The PNP accorded her all the respect her position deserves. We have all the body cam footages of her warrants being served. We have all the body cam footages of her arrival to post bail. We knew of her whereabouts the night before but we did not force the warrant of arrest.”

The Vice President, who had been critical of mainstream media, requested journalists to accompany her as she exited the building, telling them to walk in front and behind her until she got to her vehicle. She said that the “lens and mic” of the media captured the “kagarapalan (shamelessness)” of the Marcos government, apparently referring to her case.

On September 4, the court issued a warrant after it found probable cause to hold Duterte for trial. It also denied her motion to defer or recall the warrants and quash the information for lack of merit.

Duterte’s camp had argued that she could not face a criminal case while serving as Vice President because she is an impeachable official. Several legal experts, however, have said that unlike the President, the Vice President is not immune from suit.

The Department of Justice filed the three counts of grave threats in August following complaints from the National Bureau of Investigation over Duterte’s November 23, 2024, midnight press conference.

During that press conference, Duterte said she had already talked to someone who would kill Marcos, his wife, and Romualdez if she herself were killed. Duterte said at the time that she was not joking. – Rappler.com

World.title: The market eats its own: How a UP Visayas student turned Iloilo’s palengke into a horror film
World.content:
There is a shot in Kanibal that looks like nothing at all until you notice it. A woman in an orange apron works her stall. Slabs of pork hang from hooks above her head. Taped to the post behind her is a prayer card to St. Martha, patron of cooks and servants. On her chest, printed across a white campaign shirt, is the smiling face of the mayor she voted for.

By the end of the film, the meat and the woman will be difficult to tell apart.

Kanibal is a 16-minute-and-52-second Hiligaynon short film written and directed by Michael A. Baylon, a Communication and Media Studies student at the University of the Philippines Visayas. It is his debut as a director. It is also one of 20 shorts selected for the Puregold CinePanalo Film Festival 2026, each carrying a P200,000 production grant, screening in the Shorts Category (Set A) when the festival runs from September 23 to October 4 across Gateway Cineplex 18, TriNoma, Fairview Terraces, Ayala Malls Feliz, Ayala Malls Circuit, Ayala Malls Manila Bay, and Market! Market!

The premise is deceptively small. Lea (Rowen Jean Ledesma, in her introducing credit) is a meat vendor who runs her stall with her daughter Anne (Lia Sophia Sajonia) underfoot, in a public market loud with the ordinary business of a town buying and selling. One morning, her neighbor at the next stall, Anecita (Ma. Lourdes Maculada), brings news: Mayor Lin (Roselle Lao) is coming to visit. Lea has been a diehard supporter since the campaign. She is thrilled. She prepares a cut of meat as a gift.

World.title: Resil B. Mojares, National Artist for Literature, dies at 83
World.content:
Mojares was an award-winning writer, historian, and literary critic who had contributed greatly to the promotion of regional and Filipino literature

MANILA, Philippines – Renowned writer, historian, and literary critic Resil B. Mojares died on the morning of September 5, his family confirmed. Mojares had just celebrated his 83rd birthday a day earlier.

“Papa Resil was a pillar of our family, and although we will miss him dearly every day, we find comfort in knowing that he is now reunited with our dear mother, Sally, who left us in 2022. Together once again, resting peacefully in eternity,” his daughter Leigh Go Mojares wrote.

Mojares was named National Artist for Literature in 2018 alongside six other big names in arts and culture, including composer Ryan Cayabyab and cartoonist Larry Alcala.

Among the late writer’s most impactful works is the 1997 book House of Memory, a personal and cultural essay collection for which he received a Philippine National Book Award. He also authored The Feast of the Santo Niño: An Introduction to the History of a Cebuano Devotion, and Interrogations in Philippine Cultural History and The War Against the Americans: Resistance and Collaboration in Cebu, 1899-1906, to name a few.

Interrogations in Philippine Cultural History (2017) and Enigmatic Objects: Notes Towards a History of the Museum in the Philippines (2023) would be the last of his published works before his death.

In 1971, he also became a Carlos Palanca Memorial awardee, having received the second prize in the English Short Story for his work Beast in the Fields.

Mojares hails from Polanco, Zamboanga del Norte, but later moved to Cebu City, where he obtained his bachelor of arts and masters degrees from the University of San Carlos. He had served as Professor Emeritus in the same university.

The Origins and Rise of the Filipino Novel author was also the founding director of the Cebuano Studies Center, a research center on all things Cebuano culture.

Throughout his career, he was also a visiting professor at several universities across Singapore, the US, and Japan.

Literary community mourns passing of a legend

Acclaimed writer Jose “Butch” Dalisay Jr. had regarded Mojares as one of his personal heroes. The late literary great had written the blurbs for Dalisay’s short story collection Voyager and Other Fictions.

“We were friends in that rather formal way aging men assume when they sit across a table over coffee — no backslapping, no intimacies exchanged, just a wry understanding of how things work. I think the most personal we ever got was when I sent him a message condoling with him on the passing of his wife Sally a few years ago,” Dalisay wrote in a Facebook post.

“Rest up, Resil, now you can smoke and scribble all you want in that great coffeeshop in the sky.”

“Naku. Laking kawalan para sa history ng Bisayan lit. Nakikidalamhati kami sa pamilya ni Resil (What a huge loss to the history of Bisaya literature. We are grieving with Resil’s family),” fellow National Artist for Literature Virgilio “Rio Alma” Almario said in a Facebook comment.

Literary circles and organizations also joined in mourning Mojares’ death, including the Unyon ng mga Manunulat sa Pilipinas (UMPIL), which honored him with the Gawad Pambansang Alagad ni Balagtas in 1997.

Government agencies had also joined in to pay their respects for Mojares — with the National Historical Commission of the Philippines and the National Commission for Culture and the Arts remembering him for his extensive contributions to Filipino and Cebuano cultural history and literature.

Mojares was married to Salvacion “Sally” Ouano Go, with whom he shared four children. His wife passed away in 2022. – Rappler.com

World.title: Daraga in Albay equips 54 barangays with rescue vehicles
World.content:
The Daraga local government unit turns over rescue vehicles to 54 barangays to strengthen their capacity to respond to emergencies and disasters without relying solely on the MDRRMO. —Photo by Michael B. Jaucian

DARAGA, ALBAY, Philippines — Fifty-four barangays in this town have been equipped with rescue vehicles worth a total of P78 million to improve emergency response and disaster preparedness in their communities.

The vehicles, funded through the Local Government Support Fund (LGSF), were blessed by Rev. Fr. Tony Cial and turned over Friday (Sept. 4) during a ceremony at the Municipal Nursery in Barangay Gabawan led by Mayor Vic Perete and Ako Bicol Party-list Rep. Alfredo Garbin Jr.

READ: 8 Albay LGUs under calamity state amid Mayon unrest

Article continues after this 

Perete said the vehicles, equipped with fire extinguishers and other emergency equipment, would allow barangays to respond to emergencies and other incidents without having to rely solely on the Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (MDRRMO).

“We aim for zero casualty. May these rescue vehicles serve as a symbol of our continuing commitment to protect lives, strengthen disaster preparedness, and provide faster and more effective emergency response to the people of Daraga,” he said.

Perete thanked President Marcos and Ako Bicol party-list for helping facilitate the project and secure funding for the vehicles. /cb

World.title: 3 nabbed for illegal gambling in Ilocos Sur
World.content:
Inquirer files

SAN ILDEFONSO, ILOCOS SUR, Philippines — Three people were arrested for allegedly engaging in an illegal card game in Barangay Laslasong Norte, Sta. Maria in this province on Friday (Sept. 4), police said.

Personnel of the Sta. Maria Municipal Police Station, led by Lt. Jenson Refuerzo, officer in charge, acted on an intelligence report about an ongoing gambling activity in the village.

Police caught the three suspects in the act while playing “tong-its,” resulting in their arrest for alleged violation of Presidential Decree No. 1602, or the law penalizing illegal gambling.

Article continues after this 

Gambling paraphernalia seized from the suspects were inventoried and marked at the scene in the presence of two barangay officials and the arrested individuals.

Police said the operation was documented using two authorized recording devices in accordance with PNP rules and procedures.

World.title: Sara Duterte to Remulla, PNP: ‘We do not trust you’
World.content:
Vice President Sara Duterte arrives at the Quezon City Hall of Justice on Saturday, September 5, 2026, to post bail following an arrest warrant issued by Quezon City Regional Trial Court Branch 98. The warrant stems from three counts of grave threats filed against her. —Inquirer photo/Grig C. Montegrande

MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte on Saturday once more stressed her lack of trust in the police and Interior and Local Government Secretary Jonvic Remulla, whom she described as subservient to the administration.

“Wala kaming tiwala sa iyo, Jonvic Remulla, at sa mga pulis na sunod-sunuran sa isang korap na pamahalaang pinamumunuan ni Marcos,” in a statement posted on Facebook.

(“We do not trust you, Jonvic Remulla, nor the police who are subservient to a corrupt government led by Marcos.”)

Article continues after this 

READ: DILG on Duterte: We didn’t arrest her despite knowing her location

Duterte’s remarks were made after Remulla said he and the Philippine National Police (PNP) knew her whereabouts amid an arrest warrant issued to her by the Quezon City Regional Trial Court (QC RTC).

Remulla said they decided not to implement the warrant of arrest despite knowing her location the night before.

The Vice President said his pronouncement only proved the Marcos administration’s surveillance operations and harassment against her.

She further cited the PNP as among the government agencies involved.

Article continues after this 

“Ang mga salitang ito ni Secretary Jonvic Remulla ay tila nagpapatibay sa mga dokumentong matagal na naming hawak hinggil sa harassment at surveillance operations ng Philippine National Police at iba pang ahensya ng gobyerno laban sa akin,” she insisted.

(“These statements by Secretary Jonvic Remulla appear to corroborate the documents I have long held regarding the harassment and surveillance operations conducted by the Philippine National Police and other government agencies against me.”)

Article continues after this 

The Vice President even questioned how police personnel came for her family after allegedly locating her.

“Isa lamang ang malinaw na sagot—upang takutin at sindakin ang aking pamilya,” she said.

(“There is only one clear answer—to frighten and terrorize my family.”)

Duterte said that, while she recognizes the jurisdiction of the PNP, she still won’t surrender herself out of fear for her safety.

She said that the authorities cannot guarantee that she will be protected while in detention and in police custody.

“Higit sa lahat, huwag nating kalimutan ang ginawang pagkidnap ng Philippine National Police kay Pangulong Rodrigo Duterte. Pati na rin sa marami pang ginagawang harassment ng pulisya sa mga sibilyan,” she added.

(“Above all, let us not forget the kidnapping of President Rodrigo Duterte by the Philippine National Police, as well as the many other acts of harassment committed by the police against civilians.”)

Duterte further said government funds should be used to pursue and convict criminals, including public officials who accept suitcases containing the people’s money.

READ: Duterte: I was advised that posting bail is better than being detained

The Vice President posted bail early Saturday at the QC RTC for three counts of grave threats, where she told the media her worries regarding her and her family’s security.

World.title: Ilocos Sur town forms task force vs illicit tobacco trade
World.content:
Inquirer files

CALASIAO, PANGASINAN, Philippines — The municipality of San Ildefonso in Ilocos Sur has officially created a local task force to strengthen its campaign against illicit tobacco and vapor products.

The Local Anti-Illicit Trade Task Force will improve intelligence sharing, coordinate enforcement efforts and strengthen the capacity of local personnel to combat the illegal trade.

Municipal Ordinance No. 06-2026, approved on Wednesday (Sept. 2), builds on an earlier executive order issued by Mayor Amante “Tito” Purisima and establishes a permanent framework against the sale, distribution, transport, storage and possession of noncompliant or counterfeit tobacco and vapor products.

Article continues after this 

READ: NTA pushes farmer support in Ilocos tobacco areas

Local officials said the measure is particularly important because of Ilocos Sur’s strategic location and proximity to areas where illicit trade activities may emerge, including parts of Central Luzon.

The Ilocos Region has also emerged as a hotspot for illicit cigarette trading, based on Philippine National Police seizure records during the first half of 2026.

At a recent Tobacco Summit organized by the National Tobacco Administration, the PNP reported the seizure of an estimated P20 million worth of illicit cigarettes in Region I during the first six months of the year.

Widespread

A San Ildefonso resident also said vaping had become widespread in the town, particularly among students.

Article continues after this 

The ordinance was enacted following consultations with local stakeholders on the economic and social effects of illicit tobacco trade, including losses in government revenue, unfair competition against legitimate businesses and its impact on community welfare.

It defines illicit products as those without required government registrations, internal revenue stamps or graphic health warnings, as well as those sold below the minimum price prescribed by law.

Article continues after this 

Businesses will be required to comply with anti-illicit trade regulations as a condition for the issuance and continued validity of their permits. Violations may result in the suspension or revocation of permits, while major or large-volume cases may be referred to national authorities for possible action under existing laws.

The ordinance also calls for a registry of violators, training for enforcement personnel, public information campaigns, annual implementation reports and regular assessments of the municipality’s anti-illicit trade efforts.

With the new measure, San Ildefonso joins a growing number of local governments taking a more active role against illicit tobacco trade.

World.title: Solon pushes for bigger DOH budget in 2027 after massive cuts
World.content:
Inquirer files

MANILA, Philippines — Deputy Minority Leader and ACT Teachers party-list Rep. Antonio Tinio on Saturday slammed the planned cuts to the Department of Health’s (DOH) budget amid medical personnel shortages.

Under the 2027 National Expenditure Program, the health agency received a significantly lower-than-requested budget of P353.8 billion from its proposed P837 billion for next year.

During the House committee on appropriations’ briefing on the DOH’s 2027 proposed budget, Tinio raised that the massive budget reduction would affect the fund intended for hospital operations and personnel services.

Article continues after this 

READ: DOH warns of compromised programs due to possible 2027 budget cut

The solon cited that DOH hospitals in Metro Manila would receive only P26.9 billion from the previous P30 billion in 2026.

He noted that Rizal Memorial Medical Center would have a half-billion-peso loss, while the National Center for Mental Health gets a P311-million cut.

“Kulang na nga ng staff, binabawasan pa. The DOH itself admitted these are unfilled plantilla positions being removed from next year’s budget. That means hospitals will have no opportunity to fill them up during the fiscal year,” Tinio expressed.

(“There is already a shortage of staff; it is being reduced. The DOH itself admitted these are unfilled plantilla positions being removed from next year’s budget. That means hospitals will have no opportunity to fill them up during the fiscal year.”)

Article continues after this 

He expressed that filling vacant plantilla positions would address the problem of insufficient medical personnel and professionals in public hospitals.

Tinio then called for the restoration of the proposed cuts in the personnel services and maintenance and other operating expenses (MOOE) of DOH-retained hospitals.

Article continues after this 

Although the DOH said it would obtain additional funds through Philippine Health Insurance Corp (PhilHealth) reimbursements and allocations in the Medical Assistance to Indigent and Financially Incapacitated Patients (MAIFIP) program, it will still be insufficient to sustain the needs of hospitals.

Primarily, only 30,000 hospital beds remained authorized, despite the “promised expansion” of 45,000 by 2028—which was delayed because of the Health Facilities Enhancement Program budget cuts, according to Tinio.

“But reimbursement is not instantaneous. In the meantime, our hospitals will be operating on funds that are insufficient—and patients will suffer. Ang kailangan ng mga ospital, direct na pondo para direktang maibigay ang serbisyo,” he stressed.

(“But reimbursement is not instantaneous. In the meantime, our hospitals will be operating on funds that are insufficient—and patients will suffer. What hospitals need is direct funds to directly provide the service.”)

He continued, “We oppose this arrangement na mukhang pinagkakasunduan ng DBM at DOH na bawasan ang MOOE ng mga ospital dahil daw may MAIFIP at PhilHealth.”

(“We oppose this arrangement—which the DBM and DOH appear to be agreeing upon—to reduce the hospitals’ MOOE, supposedly because of the existence of MAIFIP and PhilHealth.”

He said that he would take these concerns to the plenary in a bid to seek bigger funding for the DOH.

“Maganda ang Zero Balance Billing sa papel, pero kung limitado ang kapasidad ng ating mga pampublikong ospital, limitado rin ang makikinabang na mamamayan. Iiwanan lang ng sistema ang ating mga kababayan sa mga pribadong ospital na mas mahal,” he said.

World.title: PCG probes yacht’s routes after P366M kush haul in Subic Bay
World.content:
Authorities discover more suspected high-grade marijuana from sailing yacht ‘Lindsy’ during a continuing search at the Subic Bay Yacht Club in Subic Bay Freeport, Zambales on Friday, Sept. 4, 2026. (Photo from PCG Zambales)

OLONGAPO CITY — The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) on Saturday (Sept. 5) said it is seeking access to the sailing yacht ‘Lindsy’ to examine possible clues on maritime routes used to transport illegal drugs into the country.

The boat is currently in the custody of the Bureau of Customs (BOC).

Cmdr. Euphraim Jayson Diciano, head of the PCG in Zambales, told the Inquirer that they had sent a letter to BOC-Port of Subic District Collector Geniefelle Lagmay requesting access to the yacht.

Article continues after this 

The Coast Guard wants to examine the watercraft as part of its ongoing investigation.

Diciano said the PCG will check the yacht’s voyage history, movements and navigational data to identify patterns and possible maritime corridors that may have been used to transport illegal substances.

Among the equipment and records the PCG wants to see are the yacht’s logbooks, navigational charts and onboard navigation systems.

These pieces include the boat’s electronic chart display and information system (ECDIS), chart plotter, global positioning system (GPS) and automatic identification system (AIS).

“These records will be examined to help authorities establish the yacht’s voyage history, including its movements before it arrived at Subic Bay,” Diciano said in a phone interview.

Article continues after this 

The Coast Guard said information gathered from the examination can also be incorporated into its database for future maritime law enforcement operations.

The request came as authorities continued to investigate the yacht following the discovery of alleged high-grade marijuana, or “kush,” on board the vessel at the Subic Bay Yacht Club (SBYC).

Article continues after this 

Authorities have yet to determine whether the yacht’s navigation records can establish its previous movements or shed light on possible routes connected to the shipment of illegal substances.

The total value of the suspected high-grade marijuana recovered from the yacht reached P366.6 million after authorities continued stripping and searching the vessel.

The BOC-Port of Subic confirmed on Saturday that its composite team found 109 additional packages of kush worth an estimated P204.4 million.

Authorities searched different compartments and hard-to-reach areas of the vessel, including its underside.

“Coast Guard divers also went underwater to inspect portions of the yacht as part of the continuing search for possible hidden contraband,” Diciano said.

The initial seizure followed information received by the PCG Intelligence Unit-Zambales on Sept. 1.

Mechanics repairing the yacht’s generator and engine reportedly discovered a hidden compartment containing suspected illegal substances.

This incident prompted authorities to hold covert verification and prepare an operation with the BOC and Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA).

On Sept. 2, authorities boarded and searched the yacht, recovering approximately 89 bags of suspected kush weighing 98.3 kilograms.

World.title: Kazakhstan Races to Top at World Nomad Games
World.content:
ASTANA – Kazakhstan leads the overall medal standings at the sixth World Nomad Games with 55 medals, reported the Kazakh Ministry of Tourism and Sports.

As of Sept. 4, Kazakh athletes had won 25 gold, 13 silver and 17 bronze medals.

The Kyrgyz Republic ranks second with 58 medals, including 23 gold, 24 silver and 11 bronze. Russia is third with 23 medals: four gold, six silver and 13 bronze.

Kazakhstan has won medals in audaryspak, kazakh kuresi, alysh, arm wrestling, sambo, tug of war, traditional archery, horse racing, eagle hunting and other disciplines.

Syrym Izbasarov won the audaryspak title in the 100-kilogram division. The world champion and two-time WNG winner defeated his longtime rival from the Kyrgyz Republic in the final to claim his third games title.

Daryn Otkelbai also won gold in the 90-kilogram division, while Nurzhan Erkinuly took bronze in the heavyweight category.

In the eagle hunting competition, Serikbolsyn Zhalgasuly and his hawk, Zhebe, won the gold medal. Arman Koshkarov and his golden eagle, Algyr, took silver. Kazakhstan fielded nine athletes in the eagle hunting competition.

Kazakhstan’s arm-wrestling team delivered the country’s strongest performance, winning 12 medals, including seven gold, four silver and one bronze.

Kazakh women also excelled in archery. Ayash Kabdollayeva won gold in the 60-meter puta target event, while Asemgul Galymzhanova took gold in the 40-meter Central Asian target event.

Kazakh athletes are yet to compete in 11 sports, meaning the standings could still change as the games continue.

The country also won the 300-kilometer long-distance horse race, known as zhoryk. Kazakh riders completed the four-day race first, finishing ahead of the Kyrgyz Republic.

World.title: Kazakhstan to Host Its First Ever ICAO Aviation Security Week 2026 in October
World.content:
ASTANA – Kazakhstan will host ICAO Aviation Security Week for the first time on Oct. 20-22, bringing aviation regulators, industry leaders and security experts to the capital to address emerging threats and strengthen international cooperation.

Supported by Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Transport, the event will focus on the theme Safe Skies in a Complex World: Enhancing Aviation Security for All. ICAO Council President Toshiyuki Onuma, ICAO Secretary General Juan Carlos Salazar and senior representatives of foreign states and international organizations are expected to attend, the Civil Aviation Committee reported.

Kazakhstan reports 95.7% compliance with international aviation security standards, placing it among the world’s top 20 countries and making it a regional leader in Central Asia.

Security as a foundation for aviation growth

The forum comes as Kazakhstan seeks to strengthen its position as a Central Asian aviation hub, with safety and regulatory reliability increasingly viewed as essential to competitiveness.

“The long-term sustainability of a hub depends on trust in the system: trust in safety, regulation and predictable rules,” Civil Aviation Committee Chair Saltanat Tompiyeva said in an interview with The Astana Times.

Tompiyeva, who has worked in civil aviation since 1998 and was appointed an ICAO Global Ambassador earlier this year, identified Kazakhstan’s strong aviation security and safety record as a key competitive advantage. International assessments also show 82% effectiveness of aviation safety oversight.

Addressing emerging risks

The aviation security environment is changing rapidly, with new risks linked to artificial intelligence, cyberattacks, unmanned aircraft, critical infrastructure and geopolitical instability.

Aviation Security Week will address risk management, new technologies, workforce development and stronger information-sharing mechanisms, including approaches to aviation risk assessment in conflict situations.

Discussions will be held within the framework of ICAO initiatives such as the Global Aviation Security Plan (GASeP) and the Universal Security Audit Program – Continuous Monitoring Approach (USAP-CMA).

The Astana forum will also contribute to preparations for the Third High-Level Conference on Aviation Security (HLCAS/3) in 2027.

For Kazakhstan, hosting the global forum marks a step from regional cooperation toward a stronger role in international aviation security dialogue, supporting the country’s wider ambition to develop as a regional aviation hub.

World.title: Cyberport, Astana Hub Deepen Tech Ties Between Hong Kong and Kazakhstan
World.content:
HONG KONG – Cyberport digital technology hub sees its collaboration with Kazakhstan’s Astana Hub IT park as a two-way launchpad, enabling Hong Kong to expand into Central Asia’s growing AI market while offering Central Asian startups a direct corridor into mainland China and the broader Asia-Pacific region.

Cyberport Chairman Simon Chan said Cyberport and Astana Hub share similar development priorities, particularly in finance and information technology making the hub-to-hub partnership a platform for business expansion.

In June, Cyberport signed a memorandum of understanding with Central Asian’s largest innovation clusters Astana Hub and IT Park Uzbekistan during the visit of Hong Kong business delegation to Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan, led by Chief Executive John Lee. The partnership focuses on technology transfer, supporting tech companies in areas such as AI, fintech, smart city solutions and Web 3, and facilitating overseas expansion and global market access for innovation and technology companies from both regions.

“The finance sector as well as other sectors of the economy are growing fast in Kazakhstan. There’s also a lot of business opportunities. We hope through the collaboration, our companies, stakeholders and startups can open up the business there or find the collaboration with the Kazakh business entities. Astana Hub itself is comprehensive and focused on AI,” Mr. Chan said in an interview for this story.

“Hong Kong is one of the major Asian financial centers, not only Asian but also the international financial center. We hope to build Hong Kong into an international IT hub as well. And Kazakhstan is an ideal place for our companies to open up their businesses or make collaboration with the tech companies or financial companies for more collaboration and widen their scope of business and to seek more business opportunities,” he said.

Cyberport accommodates more than 2,300 companies, including 18 listed companies with a combined market capital of more than 500 billion HK dollars (US$63 billion), nine unicorns worth more than 150 billion HK dollars (US$19 billion). Its innovation ecosystem includes AI, data science, fintech, digital assets and blockchain, cybersecurity, and smart living.

In late August, Cyberport hosted the Digital Entertainment Leadership Forum (DELF 2026) marking this direction as a strategic one.

“DELF is important not only as an event but also its content is evolving every year along with the growth of different types of technology that can be reflected in its solutions. In the past, we focused on digital entertainment and other types of technology. But nowadays, we are focusing on AI and how to incorporate it in promoting the digital entertainment industry. We use this platform to reflect the development of different types of technology and attract guests from overseas to share with us and also to share their experience and insights with our local peers and stakeholders,” said Mr. Chan.

Building a global tech network

The Hong Kong SAR government has taken major steps aligning with the nation’s 15th five-year plan on positioning Hong Kong as a hub for innovative economy in the Asia-Pacific region.

The Cyberport chairman also spoke about the qualities they look for while building connections globally.

“We hope to build a gateway or platform for the different types of companies who can access different countries and industries. The critical success factor of locating a good collaborator or good competitors is the prospects for growth. The mission of the countries or the strategy of the development strategy of the country itself. In Kazakhstan, we have agreed to help make Kazakhstan more AI-oriented.”

Diversity in tech, talent development and different funding schemes for IT building up in Hong Kong are the main advantages.

“Hong Kong welcomes our friends from overseas to open up their office or presence here. We hope for more collaboration ahead. Collaboration is pretty important as the world is changing rapidly. We are looking for more hub-to-hub cooperation to build up more opportunities for the next generations,” said Mr. Chan.

World.title: News Digest: Foreign Media Highlight Kazakhstan’s China Ties, Middle Corridor and Political Reforms
World.content:
ASTANA – The Astana Times has selected articles from global media outlets covering Kazakhstan. This week’s foreign media digest highlights President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev’s vision for deeper Kazakhstan-China cooperation, the Middle Corridor, and more.

Tokayev links Kazakhstan-China partnership to wider vision for a more connected and cooperative Eurasia

Kazakhstan President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has used the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in Bishkek and a wide-ranging interview with China’s Xinhua news agency to set out a closely connected vision of Kazakhstan’s foreign policy – combining deeper economic and technological cooperation with China with a broader commitment to multilateralism, Eurasian connectivity and reform of global institutions, reported EU Reporter on Sept. 2.

Speaking as leaders gathered in Bishkek for the 26th meeting of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) and its SCO Plus format, Tokayev presented Kazakhstan as both a committed regional partner and an increasingly active “middle power” seeking to bridge geopolitical divisions.

CPC: Total freight traffic volume along Middle Corridor increased ninefold compared to 2021

The Middle Corridor has demonstrated impressive growth dynamics in recent years, with total cargo volume transported along the route reaching 4.12 million tons by 2025, which is nine times higher than in 2021, Report informed on Sept. 1, citing an article by the Caspian Policy Center (CPC).

The author indicates that nearly all of this cargo flow passed through the Caspian Sea, making developed port infrastructure and adequate maritime capacity defining factors for the route’s viability. Delays at border crossing points and Caspian ports effectively caused an 8.4% drop in transport volumes in 2024, vividly demonstrating the acute need for infrastructure modernization.

Kazakhstan enters a new political era after historic parliamentary reform

Kazakhstan held its first parliamentary election on Aug. 23, electing 145 deputies to the country’s new Parliament, the Kurultai. The election followed a nationwide referendum in March, which approved a new Constitution that replaced Kazakhstan’s bicameral Parliament with the Kurultai. The new Constitution came into force on July 1, Euronews reported on Sept. 1.

The name of the new Parliament also had historical significance.

“Kurultai is a concept and a name that is characteristic of the steppe culture and Turkic civilisation. It reflects our national identity and shows respect for history,” said Nurgazy Anuarbekov, expert at the Kazakhstan Institute of Public Development.

President Tokayev highlights Singapore’s experience for new Astana International Airport

Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev discussed plans for a new modern airport in Astana and the use of Singapore’s aviation expertise during a meeting with Senior Minister of Singapore Lee Hsien Loong at Akorda, reported In Diplomacy on Sept. 1.

The discussion also covered political reforms, investment, transport and logistics, as well as cooperation in artificial intelligence and digitalization.

Kazakhstan completes connection section on key Middle Corridor railway line

Track connection has been completed on the Moyynty–Kyzylzhar railway line in Kazakhstan, which will become an important link in the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route (TITR or Middle Corridor), Trend reported on Sept. 3.

“The new 323.3-kilometer railway line will run through the Ulytau and Karagandy regions. Once commissioned, it will become an important link in the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route (TITR), also known as the Middle Corridor, improving regional connectivity and the efficiency of freight transportation,” the government said.

The project will shorten freight routes by 149 kilometers, reduce the load on the Moyynty-Zharyk railway section, increase the speed of container trains and expand capacity for freight and transit transportation. According to the approved schedule, the railway line is scheduled to be commissioned this year.

World.title: ChatGPT’s Kazakh Language Push Shows Why AI Must Go Beyond English
World.content:
ASTANA – ChatGPT’s growing development in the Kazakh language highlights a broader challenge for artificial intelligence: understanding a language also requires understanding the cultural context behind it, futurist and author Ron Immink told The Astana Times. Kazakhstan’s efforts to build Kazakh-language datasets and culturally specific AI benchmarks show why AI systems need to reflect the diversity of languages and cultures.

A joint project between the Qazaq Tili international association and OpenAI has developed a specialized AI Evaluation Benchmark Suite designed around the linguistic and cultural characteristics of Kazakh.

Developed originally in Kazakh rather than translated from English, the benchmark evaluates large language models on grammar, naturalness of speech, proverbs and fixed expressions, academic and literary translation, children’s literature, safety and ethnography. A separate 500-question benchmark tests knowledge of Kazakh history, traditions and culture.

The project also focuses on building the data foundation for Kazakh-language AI. The Kazakh Text Corpus has reached 14 billion tokens, covering different periods of language development and diaspora heritage, as well as education, science, technology, economics, law, medicine, history, ethnography, media and children’s content. Materials include text, audio and images.

Rauan Kenzhekhanuly, president of the Qazaq Tili international association, said during a Sept. 3 presentation that more than 10 billion tokens were initially collected from archives, museums, libraries and other sources after obtaining the necessary permissions.

The goal is to improve ChatGPT in Kazakh, including translation, information work and speech, text and audio recognition, while reducing culturally inaccurate responses.

Beyond English

The approach reflects Immink’s argument that AI development must account for cultural context.

“I think it is also going to be about context and culture. And I think we are definitely missing a trick. The problem is that most AIs are in English, but it should be in Navajo. It should be in hundreds of languages that we have. So it gets a much more deeper context,” he said.

Kazakhstan’s work demonstrates what this could mean in practice: developing AI in a language is not simply a translation exercise, but an effort to preserve the linguistic and cultural context carried by that language.

The initiative also complements Kazakhstan’s broader cooperation with OpenAI in education. Valerie Focke, OpenAI’s lead for education across Europe, the Middle East and Africa, described Kazakhstan as “a pioneer and early mover” in AI adoption and said the country was among the first globally to collaborate with OpenAI on the future of education.

As AI becomes increasingly embedded in education and everyday information access, ensuring that systems understand different languages and cultures could become important not only for technological development, but also for maintaining the digital representation of individual peoples and their cultural heritage.

World.title: EDB Launches PPP Scholarship Program at Eurasian National University
World.content:
ASTANA — The Eurasian Development Bank (EDB) has launched a scholarship program focused on public-private partnerships (PPPs) at the L.N. Gumilyov Eurasian National University (ENU), aiming to strengthen research, education and practical expertise in Kazakhstan’s PPP sector.

The initiative, unveiled on Sept. 4 alongside the opening of a new EDB-branded classroom at the university, is designed to support students interested in researching and developing PPP practices.

Under the program, students will compete for scholarships worth $600 to support their research. Recipients will also receive expert mentoring and have the opportunity to present their findings at EDB events across the bank’s member states, including the International EDB PPP Fellows Seminars.

The newly opened EDB classroom is equipped with modern multimedia technology. It will serve as a venue for lectures, seminars, project workshops, expert discussions and scientific conferences dedicated to PPPs and Eurasian integration.

“The EDB PPP scholarship program provides students with early professional orientation and helps them develop project analysis skills, while its international component enables comparative assessment of national PPP models across all EDB member states,” said Svetlana Maslova, EDB Director for PPP Projects.

“The program is designed to build a pool of specialists capable of preparing and implementing PPP projects both in Kazakhstan and across the Eurasian region. Students will gain not only academic knowledge but also a practical understanding of how real PPP projects are developed and implemented,” she added.

The Eurasian Development Bank is a multilateral development institution that finances investment projects across the Eurasian region. Since its establishment 20 years ago, the bank has focused on promoting economic integration and sustainable development among its member states.

As of the end of June 2026, the EDB’s cumulative portfolio included 348 projects with total investments of $22.1 billion. The bank’s investments are concentrated in transport infrastructure, digital systems, green energy, agriculture, industry and mechanical engineering, with a particular focus on projects that promote regional integration. Under its 2022–2026 strategy, the EDB is implementing three flagship initiatives: the Central Asian Water and Energy Complex, the Eurasian Transport Framework and the Eurasian Commodity Distribution Network.

World.title: National Bank Cuts Base Rate to 16.25% Amid Continued Disinflation
World.content:
ASTANA – The National Bank of Kazakhstan cut its base rate by 50 basis points to 16.25% on Sept. 4, as annual inflation fell below 10% after 11 consecutive months of disinflation. The regulator, however, warned that persistent inflation risks limit room for further easing.

“The balance of risks remains tilted towards inflation. Therefore, we are committed to maintaining moderately tight monetary conditions,” National Bank Governor Timur Suleimenov said.

Inflation continues to slow

Annual inflation declined to 9.8% in August, with food inflation at 9.5%, non-food inflation at 11.4% and services inflation at 8.9%. Monthly inflation remained at 0.6%, while core inflation stood at 0.7%.

Inflation expectations for the next 12 months fell to 12.1% in July, from 13.4% in June. Professional market participants continue to expect inflation of around 10% by the end of 2026.

The National Bank kept its 2026 inflation forecast at 9-11%, but raised its 2027 forecast to 6.5-8.5%, from 5.5-7.5%, citing higher external inflation, revised regulated-price assumptions and a stronger fiscal impulse.

Inflation is expected to stabilize near the 5% target in 2028.

“Our goal is not simply inflation below 10%. Our goal is sustainable and stable inflation of around 5% in 2028,” Suleimenov said.

Risks remain

The National Bank identified stronger domestic demand, fiscal stimulus, inflation expectations, fuel prices and utility tariffs among the main risks. External risks include higher global food and energy prices amid geopolitical tensions.

Tengenomika analytical Telegram channel described the decision as a continuation of easing rather than a shift to soft monetary policy.

“The National Bank continued the easing cycle. This is a normalization of the degree of tightness rather than a transition to a soft policy,” they said.

EconomyKZ.org analytical Telegram channel experts said the decision reflected a balance between declining inflation and still-strong domestic demand, with future decisions depending on whether disinflation continues.

Growth remains resilient

The National Bank maintained its 2026 GDP growth forecast at 4.5-5.5%. Kazakhstan’s economy grew 4.1% year-on-year in January-July, while non-mining GDP increased by an estimated 5.4%.

Investment in fixed capital rose 7.7%, while retail trade increased 4.1% in real terms. GDP growth is projected at 4.5% in 2027, while the 2028 forecast was raised to 4-5% from 3.5-4.5%.

The National Bank said further rate decisions would depend on inflation, domestic demand, inflation expectations, regulated prices and fiscal and quasi-fiscal stimulus.

The next scheduled decision on the base rate will be announced on Oct. 23.
